title: The planning buffer grows with the number of running implementers
description:
Xavier keeps a buffer of four planned, open, unclaimed beads and refills when it drops below two.
Both numbers are written into the role rather than derived from anything, so one implementer and
five implementers get the same queue.

**The request:** derive them from the fleet. With `n` running agents, let `m = min(2, n)`. When the
buffer drops below `m`, plan until there are `2 * m` beads in flight.

That keeps the shape of the current rule — the target is twice the floor, so the buffer still drains
by half before being refilled in one go rather than topped up on every claim — and makes both
numbers follow the fleet:

| n | m | refill below | fill to | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | nobody to build; plan nothing |
| 1 | 1 | 1 | 2 | |
| 2 | 2 | 2 | 4 | today's numbers |
| 3+ | 2 | 2 | 4 | today's numbers |

## Worth confirming: `min` caps the buffer at four

`min(2, n)` means the buffer never grows past today's four however many implementers run — it only
shrinks when fewer than two are up. That is a coherent reading of "roof": four is the ceiling, and a
small fleet gets less. It is also exactly what `max(2, n)` would not do, which would scale the buffer
up with the fleet (three implementers → refill below 3, fill to 6). The formula above is what was
asked for; this note exists so the choice is visible rather than assumed.

## Where the numbers live

- `skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md`, section *You keep a buffer of four* — the cycle, its four/two, and
  the paragraph explaining why the gap exists. Also the skill's own `description` line.
- `agents/planner.md` — the `description` frontmatter and the body, both of which say "four".

Both are in the cerebro submodule.

## For the planner to settle with the navigator

- **How Xavier counts `n`.** It is a separate session and has no fleet view. Candidates: the live
  state files in `.claude/implementers/`, `claude agents --json`, or asking Cerebro. Each has a
  failure mode — a stale state file, a session started outside Emacs — and getting `n` wrong in the
  low direction silently starves the queue.
- **Which agents count.** Implementers only, presumably — Xavier, Cerebro, Moira and Psylocke do not
  take planned beads.
- **`n = 0`.** The table says plan nothing, which is defensible and has a trap: the navigator starts
  an implementer and there is nothing for it to take, so the first thing it does is wait for Xavier.
  Whether a floor of one bead is worth keeping for that case is a judgement.
- **What happens to a buffer that is over its number** when the fleet shrinks — six planned beads
  and one implementer. Nothing needs unplanning; the rule should say so explicitly so a session does
  not invent something.
- P0 is unaffected: every unplanned P0 is planned the moment it appears, whatever the buffer says.
  Worth restating in the new wording so it does not get lost in the arithmetic.

## Validation

With one implementer running, confirm Xavier fills to two and refills when the count drops below
one. Stop it and confirm the described `n = 0` behaviour. Start two and confirm today's four/two
returns.
design:
## Context

The planner keeps "four planned, open, unclaimed beads" and refills "when the buffer drops below
two", and both numbers are literals in the role text — one implementer and five get the same queue.
Today (2026-08-15, 11:35 UTC) three implementers claimed at once from a buffer of four and the queue
went to zero; with one implementer up, four planned beads is three going stale.

**Chosen rule (the navigator's, in this planning session):** with `n` running implementers,
`m = max(2, n)`; refill when the buffer drops **below m**, and fill **to 2m**. So `n ≤ 2` is
today's 2/4 unchanged (including `n = 0`, where a floor of two waits for the first implementer to be
started); `n = 3` is 3/6; `n = 4` is 4/8. The shape — target twice the floor, so the buffer drains by
half and is refilled in one go — is kept.

**Planner's decisions:** `n` is measured from the same evidence the fleet view uses — the state
files under `.claude/implementers/` whose `pid` is alive — minus any implementer whose stop flag is
set (it finishes its bead and retires, so it will not take another planned one; an idle stop-flagged
one may still take exactly one, which is a transient under-count of one bead and harmless).
Interactive agents (Xavier, Cerebro, Moira, Psylocke) have no state file and never count. `n` is
re-measured on every pass and every wake-up, and a buffer above its number when the fleet shrinks is
left alone — nothing is ever unplanned. P0 pre-emption is untouched and restated in the new text.

**Where it lives:** the cerebro submodule (`https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro`, checked out at
`.claude/cerebro`) — `skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md`, `agents/planner.md`, `CLAUDE.md` — followed by a
submodule-pointer bump in atlantis-hud that also edits atlantis-hud's own `CLAUDE.md`. Same two-PR
delivery as ah-lyc / ah-u3i (see `bd show ah-lyc --json | jq -r '.[0].design'`). Line numbers are
against cerebro `origin/main` at `5a3df33`; ah-u3i (planned, may land first) edits `agents/implementer.md`
and `skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md`, not these files — no overlap, but rebase on cerebro `main`.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

Docs only. No code, no tests to write; the "reuse" is the existing sections, whose structure stays.

### `skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md` (cerebro)

- **Line 3, frontmatter `description`**: replace `keep four planned, unclaimed beads ahead of the
  implementers` with `keep a buffer of planned, unclaimed beads ahead of the implementers, sized
  from how many are running`.
- **Section `## You keep a buffer of four` (lines 196–229)** — rename the heading to
  `## You keep a buffer sized to the fleet` and replace lines 196–229 (heading through "Never invent
  work to hit the number.") with exactly this:

  ~~~markdown
  ## You keep a buffer sized to the fleet

  You are not here to plan one bead and leave. You keep the implementers fed, and the measure of that
  is a **buffer of planned, open, unclaimed beads** — ready for anyone to pick up — whose size follows
  how many implementers are running.

  ```bash
  # The buffer, and the only count that matters:
  bd list --label planned --status open --exclude-label human --exclude-type epic --json | jq length
  ```

  `human` is excluded because a bead waiting on the navigator is not available to an implementer, so
  counting it would starve the queue while the number looked healthy. `epic` is a split parent, which
  has children rather than a plan.

  **How many implementers are running** is `n`, measured from the same evidence the fleet view uses:
  a state file under `.claude/implementers/` whose `pid` is alive, minus any implementer whose stop
  flag is set (it finishes its bead and retires, so it will not take another). Interactive agents —
  Xavier, Cerebro, Moira, Psylocke — have no state file and never count.

  ```bash
  n=0
  for f in $(ls .claude/implementers/*.state.json 2>/dev/null); do
    name="$(basename "$f" .state.json)"
    [ -e ".claude/implementers/$name.stop" ] && continue
    pid="$(jq -r '.pid // empty' "$f" 2>/dev/null)"
    [ -n "$pid" ] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && n=$((n+1))
  done
  m=$(( n > 2 ? n : 2 )); echo "n=$n implementers, refill below $m, fill to $((2*m))"
  ```

  **The two numbers are `m = max(2, n)` and `2m`**: refill when the buffer drops **below `m`**, and
  fill **to `2m`**. Two or fewer implementers — including none — is a floor of two and a target of
  four; three is 3/6; four is 4/8. Measure `n` on every pass, since the fleet changes under you.

  The cycle:

  1. **Plan every unplanned P0**, whatever the buffer says. See *P0 pre-empts the buffer*.
  2. **Fill to `2m`.** Plan beads one at a time until the count reaches `2m`.
  3. **Sleep ten minutes.** Say that you are doing so, then wait.
  4. **Look again**, re-measuring `n`. A new P0 — plan it, always, and then continue. Otherwise:
     `m` or more in the buffer, sleep another ten minutes and look again; **fewer than `m`, fill
     back to `2m`** and start over.

  The gap between `2m` and `m` is deliberate: topping up on every single claim would have you
  planning constantly against a queue that barely moved. Let it drain by half, then refill it in one
  go.

  **The P0 check has no such gap, and that is the point.** It runs on every wake-up and acts on every
  hit — a P0 filed while you slept is planned on the next wake-up even if the buffer is untouched at
  `2m` and step 4 would otherwise have sent you straight back to sleep.

  **A buffer over its number is left alone.** When the fleet shrinks — six planned and one
  implementer — nothing is unplanned; the extra beads simply get built later. The buffer is a floor
  under the fleet, never a ceiling on planned work.

  **If you cannot reach `2m`, that is fine.** Plan every candidate there is, say how far you got and
  why, and sleep as usual — new beads arrive, and the next wake-up will find them. Never invent work
  to hit the number.
  ~~~

  The `### Sleeping without dying` subsection that follows is unchanged.
- **Lines 157–158** ("that leaves five or six planned beads instead of four, the buffer is over its
  number") → "that leaves the buffer over its `2m`, that is simply what it costs".
- **Lines 223–224** are inside the replaced block (already handled above).
- **Line 667** ("below four, plan the next one; at four, say so and sleep") → "below `2m`, plan the
  next one; at `2m`, say so and sleep", and line 669's cross-reference `See *You keep a buffer of
  four*` → `See *You keep a buffer sized to the fleet*`.
- `grep -n "four" skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md` afterwards: the remaining hits must all be about
  batching questions (lines 92, 366–368) and the "four of six" triage example (line 90) — none about
  the buffer.

### `agents/planner.md` (cerebro)

- **Line 3, frontmatter `description`**: `keeps four planned, unclaimed beads ahead of the
  implementers` → `keeps a buffer of planned, unclaimed beads ahead of the implementers, sized from
  how many are running`.
- **Line 21**: `keep four planned, open, unclaimed beads ahead of the implementers` → `keep a buffer
  of planned, open, unclaimed beads ahead of the implementers — twice the number running, and never
  fewer than four —`.
- **Line 58**: `Planning it may leave five or six beads in a buffer that wants four; that is the
  buffer being a floor, not a ceiling` → `Planning it may leave the buffer over its number; that is
  the buffer being a floor, not a ceiling`.

### `CLAUDE.md` (cerebro), line 38

`Keeps four planned beads ahead of the builders.` → `Keeps a buffer of planned beads ahead of the
builders, sized from how many are running (twice the count, never fewer than four).`

### `CLAUDE.md` (atlantis-hud), lines 107–109 — in the bump PR

`It keeps a buffer of **four planned, open, unclaimed beads** ahead of the fleet — planning the
highest-priority candidate whose blockers are already planned, sleeping ten minutes, and refilling
when the buffer drops below two.` → `It keeps a buffer of **planned, open, unclaimed beads** ahead
of the fleet, sized from the number of running implementers — twice that number, never fewer than
four — planning the highest-priority candidate whose blockers are already planned, sleeping ten
minutes, and refilling when the buffer drops below half its target.` Line 114 ("a buffer of five or
six is a price worth paying") stays — it is still true.

## Increments

1. **cerebro edits** as listed, in one commit: `docs(ah-4hr): the planning buffer follows the
   number of running implementers`. Before committing, run the `n` snippet from the new section
   in the atlantis-hud checkout (zsh and bash both) and confirm it prints a sane line — that is the
   only executable thing in this bead. `grep -rn "four planned\|buffer of four\|below two" .`
   in the cerebro root must return nothing.
2. **PR to `rmstdope/cerebro`**, `@copilot` review, every comment answered; no CI on that repo —
   say in the PR body that the change is prose plus one shell snippet, and paste the snippet's
   output. Merge, note the sha.
3. **atlantis-hud PR** from a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/ah-4hr`:
   `git submodule update --init .claude/cerebro`, then `git -C .claude/cerebro fetch origin &&
   git -C .claude/cerebro checkout <sha>`, plus the `CLAUDE.md` edit above; commit
   `docs(ah-4hr): bump cerebro to the fleet-sized planning buffer`, normal PR flow (`@copilot`,
   CI green, answered, merge). Close the bead after this merges.

## The test plan

None. Prose in a skill and an agent file, plus a shell snippet whose only check is running it. No
suite in either repository exercises these files.

## User-facing decisions

Not a player-facing surface. Settled with the navigator, since it sets how far ahead their fleet is
planned:

1. **Formula: `m = max(2, n)`, refill below `m`, fill to `2m`.** The navigator chose this in free
   text over the three offered: `min(2, n)` as the bead was filed (rejected — capped at four, and
   the buffer ran dry under three builders that same morning), `m = n` (rejected — no floor when
   nobody is running), and `min(3, n)` (rejected — ceiling of six).
2. **`n = 0` keeps two planned / fills to four** — a consequence of the formula, not a separate
   choice; the separate question was withdrawn once the formula answered it.

Planner's own calls, recorded so nobody re-opens them: `n` counts live state files minus
stop-flagged implementers; interactive agents never count; a buffer over its number is left alone;
`n` is re-measured every pass.

## Out of scope

- Any change to `cerebro.el`, the fleet view, or how implementers report themselves (ah-u3i).
- Cerebro (the orchestrator) telling Xavier `n` — Xavier measures it from the state files itself.
- Changing the ten-minute sleep, the P0 rule, or the triage step.

## Validation

- `grep -rn "four planned\|buffer of four\|below two" .` empty in the cerebro root; the same grep in
  atlantis-hud hits nothing outside `.claude/cerebro`'s history.
- Human check: with one implementer running, a fresh planner session announces `n=1 … refill below
  2, fill to 4` and fills to four; with three, `n=3 … refill below 3, fill to 6`; touch a stop flag
  and the next pass reports one fewer.

## Known traps

- **`.claude/cerebro` in the shared checkout is not where you edit.** Clone/worktree
  `rmstdope/cerebro` elsewhere and move only the pointer in atlantis-hud (ah-lyc, ah-u3i).
- **The bump must point at a sha on cerebro `main`**, not a deleted branch.
- **The planner's Bash tool is zsh** here (`(eval): no matches found` on an unmatched glob), which
  is why the snippet uses `ls … 2>/dev/null` and not a bare glob — keep that when editing it.
- **`.claude/skills/plan-bead` and `.claude/agents/planner.md` in atlantis-hud are absolute symlinks
  into the submodule**; the bump carries the change and there is nothing to edit at the link.
- **Emacs backup files (`*.md~`) are committed in cerebro** — do not edit or delete them.
- The state file gains `phase`/`phase_since` under ah-u3i; the `n` snippet reads only `pid`, so it is
  unaffected whichever lands first.
acceptance_criteria: Xavier derives its buffer from the number of running implementers: with n running and m = min(2, n), it refills when the count of planned, open, unclaimed beads drops below m, and fills to 2 * m. The four/two constants are gone from both plan-bead/SKILL.md and planner.md, including their description lines. Planning every unplanned P0 immediately is unchanged.

title: An automatic restart no longer steals the detail window
description:
An implementer finishes its bead, reports `done`, and the fleet view ends the session and starts a
fresh one for the next bead. That much is the design working. What it also does is throw the new
session into the detail window, over whatever the navigator was reading.

It happens roughly once an hour per implementer, unprompted, and with two or three of them running
it will interrupt something the navigator chose to look at.

## Where it comes from

`cerebro--supervise` handles `restart` by calling `cerebro--end-session` and then
`cerebro--launch` (`emacs/cerebro.el`). `cerebro--launch` spawns through
`cerebro--spawn-into-detail`, which exists precisely to put a new session in the detail window —
correct for `s`, where the navigator asked for that agent and expects to see it, and wrong here,
where nobody asked for anything.

So the restart inherits an intention that belongs to a keypress.

## What "in silence" should mean

Not quite "never touch the detail window". If the navigator *was* watching that agent, its session
buffer is about to be killed by `cerebro--end-session` and the window will show something else
regardless — putting the replacement there is continuity rather than theft. The distinction worth
implementing is:

- the detail window was showing that agent's session → show its replacement;
- the detail window was showing anything else → leave it alone.

Which of those two the navigator wants is worth confirming; "simply restart in silence" could also
mean the strict reading, where a restart never changes the detail window even if the buffer under it
has just been killed.

## Watch for

`cerebro--spawn-into-detail` does more than display: it binds `display-buffer-overriding-action` so
vterm cannot take the *selected* window, and wraps the spawn in `save-selected-window`. A silent
restart still needs both — a new session must not steal focus from the agent list either. Only the
"put it in the detail window" part is unwanted.

## Validation

Manual: select one agent in the detail window, then let a different implementer finish a bead and be
replaced. The detail window still shows what it did before. Then repeat while watching the
implementer that is being replaced, and confirm whatever was decided above.
design:
## Context

When an implementer reports `done`, the fleet view ends its session and starts a fresh one — and
the fresh session is thrown into the detail window, over whatever the navigator was reading.
`cerebro--supervise`'s `restart` branch calls `cerebro--end-session` then `cerebro--launch`, and
`cerebro--launch` always routes the new vterm through `cerebro--spawn-into-detail`, a function
built for the `s` keypress, where the navigator asked to see that agent. A restart inherits an
intention that belongs to a keypress.

Chosen behaviour (settled with the navigator): **continuity** — if the detail window was showing
the finished agent's own session, the replacement appears there (the buffer under the window is
about to be killed anyway; this is continuity, not theft); if it was showing anything else, the
restart touches no window. In both cases focus never leaves wherever the navigator is.

**This is the cerebro submodule** (`emacs/cerebro.el`, `https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro`).
Line numbers are against cerebro `origin/main` at `30272fa` — and **this file is hot**: ah-b8o
(window-point fix in `cerebro--tick`) and ah-lyc (list widths) are planned/in flight against the
same file, and ah-axj/ah-4xl are queued behind them. Fetch cerebro main and rebase on whatever has
merged; none of them touch these functions, so conflicts should be textual at worst.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `emacs/cerebro.el` (cerebro repo)

- **`cerebro--launch`** (line 879) gains an optional argument:

  ```elisp
  (defun cerebro--launch (agent &optional quiet)
  ```

  The only change inside: the spawn call. Today (line ~897):

  ```elisp
  (buffer (cerebro--spawn-into-detail
           session-name (lambda () (vterm session-name))))
  ```

  becomes

  ```elisp
  (buffer (if quiet
              (cerebro--spawn-quietly (lambda () (vterm session-name)))
            (cerebro--spawn-into-detail
             session-name (lambda () (vterm session-name)))))
  ```

  Everything after — the query-on-exit flag, `cerebro-session-mode`, the implementer note — is
  untouched and applies to both paths.

- **`cerebro--spawn-quietly`** — new, next to `cerebro--spawn-into-detail` (line 833):

  ```elisp
  (defun cerebro--spawn-quietly (spawn)
    "Run SPAWN without letting the buffer it makes keep any window.

  vterm displays its buffer via `pop-to-buffer-same-window', which would
  take the selected window.  `save-window-excursion' lets it do that and
  then puts every window back, so the session exists, its process runs,
  and nothing the navigator can see has changed.  Focus never moves for
  the same reason.  Returns SPAWN's buffer."
    (save-window-excursion (funcall spawn)))
  ```

  `save-window-excursion` rather than a `display-buffer-overriding-action` that returns no
  window: the no-window route depends on `pop-to-buffer` tolerating a nil window, which is
  version-sensitive, while restoring the configuration afterwards is unconditional. (See Known
  traps for the one cost.)

- **`cerebro--detail-showing-p`** — new, next to `cerebro--show-detail` (line 808):

  ```elisp
  (defun cerebro--detail-showing-p (agent)
    "Non-nil when the detail window is live and shows AGENT's session buffer."
    (and cerebro--detail-window
         (window-live-p cerebro--detail-window)
         (let ((buffer (get-buffer (cerebro--session-buffer-name agent))))
           (and buffer (eq (window-buffer cerebro--detail-window) buffer)))))
  ```

- **`cerebro--supervise`**, the `restart` branch (line 979). Today:

  ```elisp
  ('restart (cerebro--end-session agent)
            (cerebro--launch agent))
  ```

  becomes — **the check must run before the kill**, since after `cerebro--end-session` the
  window no longer shows the session:

  ```elisp
  ('restart (let ((watching (cerebro--detail-showing-p agent)))
              (cerebro--end-session agent)
              (cerebro--launch agent (not watching))))
  ```

- **`cerebro-start` (the `s` key) is untouched** — a requested start still lands in the detail
  window via the default (non-quiet) `cerebro--launch` path. Verify no other caller of
  `cerebro--launch` exists (at `30272fa` there are exactly the two: `cerebro-start` and the
  supervise restart).

### `emacs/cerebro-test.el` (cerebro repo)

Tests below; run `emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit` from
the cerebro root. Batch Emacs has a real frame, so window functions work; vterm does **not** load
in batch — the tests stub the launch layer and never call real `vterm` (the existing suite's
stubbing style, `cl-letf` on the function cells).

## Increments

1. **The predicate.** Failing test `cerebro-test/detail-showing-p-tracks-the-window`: with
   `cerebro--detail-window` bound to a window showing a buffer named as the agent's session
   buffer (`cerebro--session-buffer-name`), the predicate is non-nil; showing another buffer →
   nil; window dead or nil → nil. Then `cerebro--detail-showing-p`.
2. **Quiet spawn.** Failing test `cerebro-test/spawn-quietly-leaves-windows-alone`: record the
   window configuration (each window's buffer), call `cerebro--spawn-quietly` with a spawn that
   creates a buffer and `pop-to-buffer-same-window`s it (a stand-in for vterm's behaviour),
   assert every window shows the same buffer as before and the returned buffer exists. Then the
   function.
3. **The restart decision.** Failing test
   `cerebro-test/restart-is-quiet-unless-the-agent-was-watched`: `cl-letf` `cerebro--end-session`
   to a no-op recorder and `cerebro--launch` to record its `quiet` argument; drive
   `cerebro--supervise` with one agent whose action derives to `restart` (the existing supervise
   tests show the arrangement); with the detail window showing the agent's session buffer →
   launch called with `quiet` nil; showing something else → `quiet` non-nil; and the
   showing-check demonstrably ran before end-session (record call order). Then the branch edit
   and the `cerebro--launch` signature change.
4. **Delivery, two PRs** — the established cerebro shape (ah-b8o's plan, increment 3, is the
   template): (a) branch from cerebro `origin/main` in a worktree/clone of the cerebro repo —
   never inside `.claude/cerebro` of the shared checkout — commit
   `fix(ah-aao): an automatic restart no longer steals the detail window`, PR to
   `rmstdope/cerebro`, `@copilot` review, merge on green; (b) atlantis-hud worktree bumps the
   submodule pointer, `feat(ah-aao): bump cerebro to the quiet restart`, normal PR flow. Close
   the bead only after the bump lands in atlantis-hud main.

## The test plan

- `emacs/cerebro-test.el`: the three tests above plus the existing suite, in batch.
- No atlantis-hud suites; the bump PR runs atlantis-hud CI as usual.

## User-facing decisions

One, settled with the navigator (question tool; no mockup — the surface is window behaviour, and
the two options were described exactly):

- **Continuity over strict silence**: a restart may (only) refresh a detail window that was
  showing the restarted agent's own session; it never touches a detail window showing anything
  else, and never moves focus. Strict silence — never touching the window even when its buffer
  was just killed under it — was offered and rejected: the window would fall to an arbitrary
  buffer and the navigator would re-select by hand.

## Out of scope

- The `s` key's behaviour (requested starts still open in the detail window — that intention is
  the keypress's).
- `cerebro--spawn-into-detail` itself — unchanged; the quiet path is a sibling, not a rewrite.
- Focus/selection behaviour of `cerebro--end-session`, the stop-flag flow, and `retire`.
- Anything in atlantis-hud application code.

## Validation

- ERT suite green in batch, new tests red-then-green in order.
- Human check, real fleet view with two implementers up: select agent A's session into the detail
  window, wait for agent B to finish a bead and restart — the detail window still shows A;
  then watch B itself and let it restart — the detail window shows B's fresh session; in both
  cases point stays where it was.

## Known traps

- **Check before kill.** `cerebro--detail-showing-p` is meaningless after `cerebro--end-session`
  has killed the buffer — the window will already show a replacement buffer. The `let` ordering
  in the restart branch is the fix's load-bearing line; increment 3's call-order assertion pins
  it.
- **`save-window-excursion` restores windows, not buffer existence** — exactly what is wanted;
  but it means the selected window *briefly* shows the new session during the spawn. In an
  interactive session this can flash for a frame. Accepted: the alternative
  (`display-buffer-no-window` + `allow-no-window`) depends on `pop-to-buffer` tolerating a
  windowless display, which varies by Emacs version; do not switch to it without testing on the
  navigator's Emacs.
- **vterm does not load in batch** — `cerebro--launch` `user-error`s without it. The tests stub
  `cerebro--launch`/spawn thunks and never touch real vterm; do not try to install vterm in CI.
- **The file is hot.** ah-b8o (`cerebro--tick`) and ah-lyc (formats/widths) land in the same file
  around the same time; fetch cerebro main before branching and rebase before the PR. No shared
  functions — conflicts, if any, are textual.
- **Two-PR delivery**: the fix is invisible to the running fleet until the submodule bump merges
  in atlantis-hud; the bead closes on the bump, not on the cerebro merge.
acceptance_criteria: When the fleet view replaces a finished implementer, the detail window keeps showing whatever it was showing, unless it was showing that agent's own session. Focus does not move: the navigator stays in whichever window they were in. Starting an agent with s still shows it in the detail window as it does today.
close_reason: Delivered in rmstdope/cerebro#13, atlantis-hud#253 (submodule bump), and atlantis-hud#254 (retrospective)

title: Warnings tab: each advisory order check on and off from settings
description: The user-facing half of ah-m9q: a Warnings settings tab with one toggle per advisory check, grouped Teaching/Resources/Guarding, global scope, off = not produced by the core. Absorbs the Global tab's unguarded-hex checkbox. All wording chosen by the navigator; see the parent and the mockup.
design:
## Context

The advisory order checks — teaching, resources, guarding — are suggestions, and which are useful
depends on how somebody plays. This bead gives each of the eight advisory codes its own on/off
toggle in a new **Warnings** settings tab, grouped Teaching / Resources / Guarding, global in
scope, with **off meaning the core does not produce the finding at all** (the `hex-unguarded`
precedent — counts, chip, panels and editor always agree, nothing anywhere says "hidden"). The
Global tab's "Warn about unguarded hexes" checkbox is absorbed by the new tab, keeping its
off-by-default. Every wording shipped here was chosen by the navigator; the mockup is
`docs/ui/warning-toggles.html` (merged in PR #249) and its "Decisions" paragraph is the record.

**This bead builds on ah-m9q.1** ("Order-check options cross the validation wire as one object"),
which is planned but may not be built yet. That bead creates the seam this plan cites:
`codes::ALL` and `CheckOptions::emits(code)` in `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`,
`ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES` / `AdvisoryCheckCode` / `OrderCheckOptions.disabledCodes` in
`packages/core-client/src/index.ts`, and a wire that carries a `disabled_codes` list end to end.
**Those names are promises from ah-m9q.1's plan, not yet facts** — read that bead's design (and
the merged code, once it lands) before starting, and verify each name at its cited site.

Line numbers for existing code are against `origin/main` at `4414626`; ah-m9q.1 will have moved
some of them.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — gate every advisory emission

ah-m9q.1 gates only `hex-unguarded`. Wire `options.emits(...)` through the remaining emission
sites (at `4414626`: lines 667, 679, 721, 758, 817, 827, 846, 861, 931 — re-locate after
ah-m9q.1's constants replace the literals), each as an early guard in the same shape as the
existing one at 761. Prefer gating at the emission site over skipping whole check functions:
`check_one_teacher` emits four different codes and a player may want some of them.

### `packages/shared/src/settingsStore.ts` — one record, not eight booleans

Follow the store's five-list pattern (field, setter, `Persisted` pick, `DEFAULTS`, `partialize`)
**once**, with a record:

```ts
import { ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES, type AdvisoryCheckCode } from "@atlantis/core-client";

export type AdvisoryChecks = Record<AdvisoryCheckCode, boolean>;

// SettingsState:
advisoryChecks: AdvisoryChecks;
setAdvisoryCheck: (code: AdvisoryCheckCode, enabled: boolean) => void;
// DEFAULTS:
advisoryChecks: DEFAULT_ADVISORY_CHECKS,   // every code true except "hex-unguarded": false
```

- Export `DEFAULT_ADVISORY_CHECKS` and a reconciler
  `reconcileAdvisoryChecks(stored: unknown): AdvisoryChecks` that starts from the defaults and

  persisted under `"atlantis-hud-settings"`. In the reconciler/merge path: when the stored blob

  `advisoryChecks["hex-unguarded"]` from it. The old field and its setter
  (`warnOnUnguardedHex` at 79, `setWarnOnUnguardedHex` at 106/278-280, picks at 122/240/318) are

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/settingsTabs.ts`

- `SettingsTabId` (line 9): add `"warnings"`.
- `SETTINGS_TABS` (18–23): `{ id: "warnings", label: "Warnings" }` **between "Per game" and

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingToggle.tsx` — new, extracted first

`GlobalSettings` repeats one checkbox-row shape five times (`SettingsDialog.tsx:237-250, 258-274,
281-296, 350-365, 367-382`). Extract it before adding nine more, following the
`UnitListLimitStepper.tsx` precedent (own file, own test):

text-ink-soft">`, title `block`, description `block text-[10px] text-ink-dim`, checkbox

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.tsx`

- Panel dispatch (132–142): add `{tab === "warnings" ? <WarningSettings /> : null}`.
- New local `WarningSettings` component beside `GlobalSettings` (183): three group headings and

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx`

- The settings selector at line 512 reads `advisoryChecks` instead of `warnOnUnguardedHex`.
- Both validation call sites (2002–2003 and 2132–2133, as reshaped by ah-m9q.1) build
  `disabledCodes` from the record:
  `ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES.filter((code) => !advisoryChecks[code])`.
- **Both effect dependency arrays** (2022 and 2160–2172) carry `advisoryChecks` — the record is
  replaced immutably by `setAdvisoryCheck`, so identity changes exactly when content does. Miss
  either array and a flipped toggle leaves stale diagnostics until the next keystroke (the
  survey's one warning about this pipeline).

## Increments

1. **`SettingToggle` extraction.** Failing test `SettingToggle.test.tsx`: renders title,
   description, `aria-label`, testid; change fires `onChange` with the flipped value. Then the
   component and the four remaining `GlobalSettings` conversions (strings and testids
   unchanged; existing smoke stays green).
2. **Store.** Failing tests in `settingsStore.test.ts`, beside the existing pair at lines 70/76:
   `"advisory checks default to on, except the unguarded-hex one"`;
   `"persists a toggled advisory check"` (round-trip via `persist.rehydrate()`);
   `"reconciles garbage advisory values to the defaults"`;
   `"migrates the old unguarded-hex preference into the record"` (seed a blob containing
   `warnOnUnguardedHex: true` under `"atlantis-hud-settings"`, rehydrate, assert
   `advisoryChecks["hex-unguarded"] === true`). The two old tests at 70/76 are replaced by these,
   not kept. Then the record, setter, defaults, reconciler, migration, and the old field's
   removal.
3. **Rust gates.** Failing test in `semantics.rs` `mod tests`:
   `every_advisory_code_can_be_silenced` — for each code in `codes::ALL`, run a fixture known to
   emit it (reuse the existing per-check test fixtures) with that code disabled and assert it is
   absent while at least one other still-enabled fixture's finding survives; plus
   `a_disabled_code_silences_both_its_emission_sites` for `not-enough-silver` (unit-level and
   shared-purse). Then the eight remaining `emits()` gates.
4. **Tab + panel.** Failing tests: `settingsTabs.test.ts` — update the four enumerating
   assertions (lines 5–31) to the new five-tab order `["global","game","warnings","snippets",
   "about"]`, red first. New `SettingsDialog`-side coverage in `WarningSettings` terms: a
   DOM test asserting the nine toggles render with their exact titles, grouped under the three
   headings, and that `settings-warning-hex-unguarded` starts unchecked while the rest start
   checked. Then the tab entry, `WarningSettings`, the moved checkbox's removal from
   `GlobalSettings`, and the AppShell wiring.
5. **Smoke.** In `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts`: rewrite the `warnAboutUnguardedHexes` helper
   (lines 954–958) to open Settings, click `settings-tab-warnings`, check
   `settings-warning-hex-unguarded`, Escape — its two dependent tests (960, 991) then pass
   unchanged. New test `"a silenced advisory check disappears everywhere at once"`: load the
   turn-71 fixture that produces the silver warning (the `:909` test is the model), assert the
   warning is present in `orders-diagnostics` and the `problems-chip` count; open Settings →
   Warnings, untick "Overspent silver"; assert the diagnostic leaves the editor list, the chip
   count drops (or the chip unmounts), and `region-problems` no longer lists it; re-tick and
   assert it returns. In `tests/smoke/settings.spec.ts`: extend the tab-navigation coverage to
   the fifth tab if a test enumerates tabs.

## The test plan

- `SettingToggle.test.tsx`, `settingsStore.test.ts`, `settingsTabs.test.ts`, the
  `WarningSettings` DOM test — `pnpm -C packages/shared test`.
- `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core` — increment 3.
- Smoke: the rewritten helper's two tests, the new end-to-end toggle test, `settings.spec.ts` —
  `pnpm run test:smoke`.
- `pnpm run check` before the PR.

## User-facing decisions

Mockup: `docs/ui/warning-toggles.html` (PR #249; its "Decisions" paragraph is the record). The
interview, held on the parent ah-m9q before the split:

1. **Grouped (variant A)** — Teaching / Resources / Guarding headings — chosen over a flat nine
   (rejected: the teaching five become noise to scan past).
2. **Global scope** — chosen over per-game (rejected for now: "per game" is not a settings scope
   today; building per-game persistence for this would be its own bead).
3. **Off = not produced by the core** — the `hex-unguarded` precedent — chosen over
   produced-but-hidden with an "N hidden" count (rejected: a brand-new client filter mechanism
   and two sources of truth; nothing filters by code today).
4. **Tab labelled `"Warnings"`, between Per game and Snippets**; the Global tab's unguarded-hex
   checkbox **moves** into it, off-by-default kept — one mechanism, as the bead itself warned.
5. **Defaults: everything on except Unguarded hexes** — today's behaviour exactly.
6. **All nine titles and descriptions verbatim** as tabled above and in the mockup ("Yes, all as
   shown" — the navigator approved the wording wholesale).
7. Editor underlines follow for free: an off check emits nothing, so nothing underlines — the
   bead's open question about `orderLint.ts` dissolves under decision 3.

## Out of scope

- Per-game scoping of these toggles (future bead if wanted).
- The parser's `unknown-item` warning and all syntax diagnostics — never toggleable; turning
  those off would hide a broken turn.
- Any "N hidden warnings" indicator anywhere (explicitly rejected).
- `role="tabpanel"`/`aria-controls` wiring for the dialog — a real gap the survey found, but a
  behaviour change to all five tabs; file it as its own bead if wanted rather than smuggling it
  in here.
- The wire itself — ah-m9q.1.

## Validation

- `pnpm run check` green.
- Human check: open Settings — five tabs, Warnings third; the Global tab no longer shows the
  unguarded-hex checkbox; Warnings shows three groups, nine toggles, Unguarded hexes alone
  unticked; with the turn-71 fixture loaded, untick "Overspent silver" — the warning vanishes
  from the editor's list, the header chip and the region panel within a second; re-tick — it
  returns; reload — the choice survives; a player who had the old checkbox ticked still gets
  unguarded-hex warnings after upgrading (migration).

## Known traps

- **ah-m9q.1 is a promise until merged.** `codes::ALL`, `CheckOptions::emits`,
  `ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES`, `disabledCodes` are defined in its plan, not yet on main at `4414626`.
  If it merged first (the dependency edge says it must), read the merged code and reconcile any
  drift before citing it in tests.
- **Migrate, don't clamp** — this repository has paid for that before. The old
  `warnOnUnguardedHex: true` in a persisted blob must become `advisoryChecks["hex-unguarded"]:
  true`; silently applying the new default would flip a setting the player chose.
- **Both dependency arrays or stale diagnostics** — `AppShell.tsx:2022` *and* the import
  effect's array (2160–2172). The survey flagged this as the one way the feature half-works.
- **Keep `setAdvisoryCheck` immutable** (`set({ advisoryChecks: { ...prev, [code]: enabled } })`)
  — the effect deps rely on record identity.
- **The five existing Global toggles keep their exact testids and strings** through the
  `SettingToggle` extraction — `settings-warn-unguarded` is the only one that disappears, and
  only because its control moves; `startup-help.spec.ts` and `settings.spec.ts` reference the
  others.
- **`settingsTabs.test.ts` breaks by design** (four enumerating assertions) — update them to the
  new order in the same increment as the tab, red first.
- **The dialog has no tabpanel ARIA** — do not "fix" it here (see Out of scope); the new panel
  follows the existing pattern, a bare div under the tablist.
- **Smoke's `warnAboutUnguardedHexes` helper** is used by two tests that assert unrelated
  behaviour — rewrite the helper, not the tests.

title: The bead panel marks its selection with the cursor alone, like the agent list
description:
The two tables in the fleet view mark their selection differently, and one of them is heavier than
the navigator wants.

- **Agent list** (`cerebro-mode`): nothing but the cursor. In the window you are in, that is a solid
  block; in a window you are not in, Emacs draws a hollow box, because
  `cursor-in-non-selected-windows` is `t` by default.
- **Bead panel** (`cerebro-beads-mode`): `hl-line-mode` with `hl-line-sticky-flag` set, so the whole
  row carries a background colour and keeps it when the navigator is elsewhere
  (`emacs/cerebro.el`, in the mode body).

**The request:** drop the background. Mark both tables with the cursor alone.

## Why the panel got the background, and why that reason is weaker than it looked

The panel was given `hl-line` deliberately: the bead panel is the window the navigator is usually
*not* in — they are in the agent list, or typing to an agent in the detail window — and a mark that
only shows where the focus is would not have answered "which bead have I picked" from anywhere else.

That reasoning overstated the case. A hollow-box cursor *is* drawn in non-selected windows by
default, so the mark was never actually invisible, only quieter. Whether quieter is too quiet for a
row of small text at the bottom of a narrow column is a matter of taste, and is what this bead is
asking.

## Scope

Remove `hl-line-mode` from `cerebro-beads-mode`, leaving both tables marked by the cursor. Nothing
else about the selection changes: the bead panel still tracks its selection by bead id across a
refresh, and still restores `window-point` so the mark lands where the navigator can see it.

## For the planner to settle with the navigator

- If the hollow-box cursor turns out to be too faint in the panel, the fallback is a marker in the
  text itself — a `>` in a gutter column, say — rather than bringing the background back. Worth
  deciding up front which way to jump, since it is the same question either way.
- Does anything depend on `cursor-in-non-selected-windows` being left at its default? A navigator
  who has set it to `nil` in their own config would lose the mark entirely in both tables, where
  today the panel would still show one.

## Validation

Manual: with a bead marked, move to the agent list and confirm the bead's row has no background and
the position is still discernible. Then the reverse: with an agent selected, look at the agent list
from the panel.
design:
## Context

The fleet view's two tables mark their selection differently: the agent list (`cerebro-mode`) with
nothing but the cursor, the bead panel (`cerebro-beads-mode`) with `hl-line-mode` and
`hl-line-sticky-flag`, so the selected bead's whole row carries a background colour that persists
when the navigator is in another window. The navigator asked for the background to go: **both tables
marked by the cursor alone**, which in a non-selected window is the hollow box Emacs draws by default
(`cursor-in-non-selected-windows` is `t`).

Settled with the navigator (see *User-facing decisions*): the Emacs default hollow box, nothing set
buffer-locally; if it proves too faint in use, the agreed follow-up is
`(setq-local cursor-in-non-selected-windows 'box)` in both modes — never the background back, never
a text marker.

**Where the code lives:** the cerebro submodule (`https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro`, checked out
at `.claude/cerebro`), then a submodule-pointer bump in atlantis-hud — the two-PR delivery of ah-lyc /
ah-axj / ah-u3i (`bd show ah-lyc --json | jq -r '.[0].design'`). Line numbers are against cerebro
`origin/main` at `5a3df33`. ah-u3i and ah-aao (both planned/in flight) also edit `emacs/cerebro.el`,
in other functions — rebase on cerebro `main` before the PR.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `emacs/cerebro.el` (cerebro)

- **`cerebro-beads-mode`, lines 1423–1431.** Delete the two forms
  `(setq-local hl-line-sticky-flag t)` and `(hl-line-mode 1)` **and** the four-line comment above
  them ("The mark has to stay visible when the navigator is in another window …"). Replace the
  comment with this one, so the next reader knows the background was removed on purpose and what the
  fallback is:
  ```elisp
  ;; No `hl-line-mode' here, deliberately (ah-4xl): the mark is the cursor
  ;; alone, as in the agent list - a hollow box in a window the navigator is
  ;; not in, since `cursor-in-non-selected-windows' defaults to t. If that
  ;; ever proves too faint, the agreed next step is
  ;; (setq-local cursor-in-non-selected-windows 'box) in both modes, not a
  ;; row background.
  ```
  The mode body keeps `revert-buffer-function` and `truncate-lines`. Nothing else in the file
  references `hl-line` (`grep -n hl-line emacs/cerebro.el` must return nothing afterwards).
- **Untouched, and worth knowing why it still works**: `cerebro--beads-render` (lines ~1319–1352)
  re-finds the selected bead by id and pushes `window-point` into every window showing the panel; the
  cursor is what the navigator now sees, so that loop is what keeps the mark on the right row after
  each thirty-second redraw. `cerebro--goto-bead` (line 1274) and `cerebro--move-bead` leave point at
  the beginning of the row — the two-column prefix (`"  "` or `"↻ "`), so the hollow box lands on a
  blank cell, as it does in the agent list's padding column.

### `emacs/cerebro-test.el` (cerebro)

- **`cerebro-test/a-bead-is-marked-from-the-first-render`, line 1142** — currently asserts
  `(should hl-line-mode)`. Change that one line to `(should-not (bound-and-true-p hl-line-mode))`
  and the docstring to "Point starts on a bead rather than on the header above it, and the mark is
  the cursor alone - no hl-line background (ah-4xl)." `bound-and-true-p`, because with the mode
  never turned on in that buffer the variable may not be buffer-local yet.
- Nothing else: the selection-by-id and window-point tests (`the-selected-bead-survives-a-refresh`,
  the `*cerebro-test-window-point*` test at ~1204) do not mention hl-line and must stay green.

### Docs

None mention `hl-line` or the row background (checked `docs/`, `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`,
`agents/orchestrator.md`).

## Increments

1. **RED**: edit the test as above; `emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit`
   from the cerebro root — that one test fails (`hl-line-mode` is `t`). **GREEN**: the mode-body
   change. Whole suite green.
2. **Delivery, two PRs.** (a) cerebro: `fix(ah-4xl): the bead panel marks its selection with the
   cursor alone`, PR to `rmstdope/cerebro`, `@copilot` review, every comment answered; no CI on
   that repo — paste the ERT run into the PR body. Merge, note the sha. (b) atlantis-hud worktree
   under `.claude/worktrees/ah-4xl`: `git submodule update --init .claude/cerebro`, then
   `git -C .claude/cerebro fetch origin && git -C .claude/cerebro checkout <sha>`; commit
   `fix(ah-4xl): bump cerebro to the cursor-only selection mark`; normal PR flow. Close the bead
   after (b) merges.

## The test plan

- cerebro ERT: the amended `cerebro-test/a-bead-is-marked-from-the-first-render` plus the whole
  suite, in batch. Nothing in atlantis-hud's suites is touched; the bump PR runs atlantis-hud CI as
  usual.

## User-facing decisions

Settled with the navigator via ASCII previews in the question tool (a terminal table; no HTML
mockup):

1. **The mark in a non-selected window is Emacs's default hollow box** — nothing set. Rejected: a
   forced solid block (`(setq-local cursor-in-non-selected-windows 'box)` in both modes — heavier,
   and overrides the navigator's own global setting) and a `>` written into the row text (more code:
   a redraw on every move). Consequence, accepted: a navigator who sets
   `cursor-in-non-selected-windows` to `nil` globally loses the mark in both tables.
2. **If it proves too faint, the follow-up is the solid block (`'box`)** — recorded here so it is not
   re-argued. Rejected as fallbacks: the `>` text marker, and restoring `hl-line-mode` in the panel.

## Out of scope

- Any change to the agent list's mark (it already is the cursor alone).
- Selection tracking by id, `window-point` restoration, `n`/`p` movement — unchanged.
- Faces, glyphs, column widths (ah-lyc, ah-u3i).

## Validation

- ERT suite green in batch, run from the cerebro clone (not from `.claude/cerebro` in the shared
  tree — `-L emacs` loads whichever tree you are in).
- Human check after the bump: `M-x cerebro`, `RET` into the bead panel, mark a bead, `C-x o` back to
  the agent list — the bead's row has no background and shows a hollow box at its left edge; wait
  thirty seconds (a panel redraw) — the box is still on that bead. Then the reverse: from the panel,
  the agent list's selected row shows its hollow box.

## Known traps

- **`.claude/cerebro` in the shared checkout is not where you edit.** Clone/worktree
  `rmstdope/cerebro` elsewhere; move only the pointer in atlantis-hud.
- **The bump must point at a sha on cerebro `main`**, not a deleted branch.
- **`emacs --batch` in the wrong tree tests the wrong file** — run it in the cerebro clone.
- **`*.el~` backup files are committed in cerebro** — do not edit or delete them.
- Two other beads touch `emacs/cerebro.el` right now (ah-u3i, ah-aao) — expect a rebase; there is no
  overlap with the mode body.
acceptance_criteria: The bead panel marks its selected row with the cursor and no background colour. The agent list is unchanged. Both tables mark the selection the same way. The panel still keeps its mark on the same bead across a refresh, and still moves window-point so the mark is where the navigator can see it.

title: The whole row of an asking agent is emphasised in the fleet list
description:
Most of this already works, and the bead exists for the part that does not.

## What the fleet list does today

An agent blocked on a question the navigator has to answer shows the state `asking`, and
`emacs/cerebro.el` already marks it three ways:

- a `?` glyph in place of the status dot, in `warning` face;
- the word `asking` in the State column;
- **bold** on the Agent, Role and State columns.

Rendered:

    col 0 "? Storm"      bold
    col 1 "implementer"  bold
    col 2 "asking"       bold
    col 3 "ah-a1b"       not bold
    col 4 "16m"          not bold

## The gap

The navigator asked for the **entire row**. The Bead and For columns are not emphasised, so the row
trails off into normal weight at exactly the point where it says which bead is stuck and how long it
has been waiting — the two facts most worth reading once the row has caught the eye.

`cerebro--entry` applies `cerebro--emphasize` to three of the five columns. Extending it is small.
Making it *read* well may not be: bold across a full row in a narrow window is a heavier mark than
bold on a name, and the reason only three columns carry it today was to keep bold meaning "this row
wants you" without shouting.

## Worth confirming before building

Whether an implementer ever actually writes `asking` to its state file in practice. The
`implement-bead` skill instructs it to, before putting a question to the navigator, but if no agent
has yet done so then this whole signal has never fired for real and the first thing to fix is that,
not the styling.

## For the planner to settle with the navigator

- Whole row bold, or bold plus a background (`hl-line`-style) on the row, or the row in a face of
  its own so a theme can tune it?
- Should `done` — the other transient state — get any emphasis, or does bold stay exclusive to
  "needs you"?

## Validation

Manual: with an implementer in `asking`, confirm every column of its row is emphasised, and that a
`working` row beside it plainly is not.
design:
## Context

An agent in `asking` is blocked on the navigator, and the fleet list already marks it three ways:
the `?` glyph (warning face), the word `asking`, and **bold** on the Agent, Role and State columns
(`cerebro--emphasize`, keyed on `cerebro--wants-attention-p`, which is `(eq state 'asking)` —
`emacs/cerebro.el:216`). The Bead and For columns stay plain, so the row trails off into normal
weight exactly where it says which bead is stuck and for how long. The navigator chose: **bold the
whole row, and bold stays exclusive to `asking`** — no colour change, no emphasis for `done`.

**Cerebro submodule** (`emacs/cerebro.el`, `https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro`). Line numbers
against cerebro `origin/main` at `30272fa`. **The exact lines this bead edits are also edited by
ah-lyc** (planned, likely in flight): ah-lyc rewrites `bead-col` (external `—`, ellipsis
truncation) and shrinks the column widths. Fetch cerebro main first and build on whatever has
merged — if ah-lyc landed, wrap its versions of the cells; if not, expect a rebase.

One verification the bead itself asks for, kept cheap: the `asking` protocol exists end to end —
`implement-bead`'s skill instructs writing `asking` to the state file (SKILL.md:74, 235) and
`cerebro--derive` maps the string at `cerebro.el:129` — so this is styling, not plumbing. No
plumbing work is in scope; if a live implementer is seen never to reach `asking` in practice,
that is a separate bead against the implementer skill, not this one.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `emacs/cerebro.el` (cerebro repo)

`cerebro--entry` (lines ~236–257). `attention` is already computed (line ~244); apply
`cerebro--emphasize` to the last two cells exactly as the first three do:

- `bead-col` (~251–254): wrap the *whole* resulting string —
  `(cerebro--emphasize <today's cond expression> attention)`. This composes with ah-lyc's `—` and
  truncation unchanged: emphasize takes the finished string.
- `for-col` (~255): `(cerebro--emphasize (if external "" (cerebro--elapsed ...)) attention)` —
  emphasizing `""` is a no-op, so the external case needs no special path.

Nothing else changes: `cerebro--wants-attention-p` already excludes `done` (and everything else),
which is precisely the "asking only" decision.

### `emacs/cerebro-test.el` (cerebro repo)

One test beside the existing entry tests (`cerebro-test/entry-working-implementer-shows-bead-and-elapsed`
and friends). Run: `emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit`.

## Increments

1. **Failing test.** `cerebro-test/entry-asking-emphasises-every-column` — build an `asking`
   agent with a bead and a since-time, call `cerebro--entry`, and assert all five cells of the
   vector carry the bold face that `cerebro--emphasize` applies, while the same agent in
   `working` has it on none. Read faces with `get-text-property 0 'face` (or the property
   `cerebro--emphasize` actually sets — read that function first and assert on what it does, not
   on an assumed `'bold`).
2. **The fix** — the two `cerebro--emphasize` wraps. Suite green.
3. **Delivery, two PRs** — the established cerebro shape (see ah-b8o's plan, increment 3, for the
   exact commands): cerebro-repo PR `fix(ah-axj): the whole row of an asking agent is emphasised`,
   `@copilot` review, merge; then the atlantis-hud submodule bump
   `feat(ah-axj): bump cerebro to the full-row asking emphasis`. If ah-lyc/ah-aao/ah-b8o are
   mid-flight in the same file, coordinate: rebase, and the bump PR may name several beads' shas —
   bump to the latest cerebro main containing this fix.

## The test plan

- `emacs/cerebro-test.el`: the new test plus the untouched suite, in batch.
- No atlantis-hud suites; the bump PR runs CI as usual.

## User-facing decisions

Settled with the navigator (question tool with rendered row previews; no HTML mockup — the
surface is a terminal table and the previews showed the exact rows):

1. **Bold across the whole row** — chosen over bold + warning-face colour (rejected: colours a
   full line of the list; the `?` glyph already carries the colour) and over a dedicated
   `cerebro-asking` face (rejected: same look today, one more moving part).
2. **`asking` only** — `done` stays plain; bold keeps meaning "this row wants you". Emphasising
   `done` was offered and rejected as diluting the signal.

## Out of scope

- Any change to `cerebro--wants-attention-p`, the glyphs, faces, or the `asking` state protocol.
- The bead panel's styling.
- Fixing an implementer that never writes `asking` (separate bead if observed).

## Validation

- ERT suite green in batch; the new test red before, green after.
- Human check, real fleet view: an implementer in `asking` shows every one of its five cells
  bold, including Bead and For; the `working` row beside it is plain; a `done` row is plain.

## Known traps

- **ah-lyc edits the same two expressions.** Its plan turns `(external)` into `—` and truncates
  long ids; this bead wraps whichever version is on main. The wrap-the-finished-string shape
  survives both orders; a mid-air collision is a rebase, not a redesign.
- **Assert on what `cerebro--emphasize` actually applies** — read it before writing the test;
  asserting a guessed face name fails against propertize details. ah-lyc's plan carries the same
  warning about faces and `substring-no-properties` for content assertions.
- **Emphasizing the empty string** (external's For cell) must stay harmless — it is, since
  `cerebro--emphasize` on `""` returns `""`; do not add a conditional for it.
- **Two-PR delivery** — the bead closes when the atlantis-hud submodule bump merges, not when
  the cerebro PR does.
acceptance_criteria: In the fleet list, every column of an agent in the asking state is emphasised, including Bead and For. A row in any other state carries no emphasis, so the mark still means "this one wants you". The ? glyph keeps its own colour rather than being repainted by the row emphasis.

title: Per-agent bd actor identity so two implementers cannot claim the same bead
description:
On 2026-08-14 ~22:55Z, Cyclops claimed ah-3cs and Storm — started 42 seconds later — claimed the same bead successfully sixteen seconds after Cyclops's claim landed. Both then built in the same worktree (.claude/worktrees/ah-3cs) until the navigator noticed and Storm was stood down.

Root cause: every agent on this machine runs under the same bd actor (the local git identity, Henrik Kurelid). `bd update --claim` is documented as idempotent when the bead is already claimed by you — so the second agent's claim returns success instead of exiting 13, and both sessions heartbeat the same lease, making the duplication invisible from the outside (the assignee reads identically either way).

Wanted: each implementer session claims under a distinct actor identity — e.g. the launcher (.claude/cerebro/scripts/run-implementer and the cmux launch path) exporting the agent name as bd's user/actor before the session starts — so a second claim on an already-claimed bead fails (exit 13) and the agent picks different work or waits. Note --if-assignee cannot combine with --claim, so identity is the mechanism, not guard flags. Also worth covering: what Cerebro's sweeps and bd reclaim see once assignees carry agent names instead of a human name.

Urgency argument: this silently doubles work and corrupts a shared worktree whenever two implementers start near-simultaneously with a short queue — exactly the normal fleet-startup case.
design:
## Context

On 2026-08-14 ~22:55Z Cyclops claimed ah-3cs and Storm, started 42 seconds later, claimed the same
bead successfully and both built in the same worktree until the navigator stood Storm down. Root
cause: every session on this machine runs bd as the same actor — bd's global `--actor` flag defaults
to `$BEADS_ACTOR`, then `git user.name` ("Henrik Kurelid"), then `$USER` — and `bd update --claim`
is idempotent when the bead is already claimed *by you*, so the second claim succeeded silently and
both sessions heartbeated one lease.

**The fix is one mechanism**: the launchers export `BEADS_ACTOR=<agent name>` before `exec claude`,
so every bd invocation inside a launched session carries that agent's identity. Both implementer
launch paths funnel through `scripts/run-implementer` (the terminal invocation, and the Emacs fleet
view — `cerebro--launch-command`, `emacs/cerebro.el:267-278`, returns that script plus the name), so
one export covers both. The bead description's mention of a "cmux launch path" is stale — nothing
named cmux exists anywhere in the repository or the submodule.

**Verified behaviour with distinct actors** (planner ran this experiment against the live bd on
2026-08-15, scratch bead ah-dzj, since closed):

- `BEADS_ACTOR=Storm bd update <id> --claim` on a bead held by Cyclops → **exit 1**, stderr
  `Error updating <id>: issue already claimed by Cyclops`. (The bead description guessed exit 13;
  that code belongs to `--if-assignee`/`--if-status` guard mismatches, not to claim contention.
  Claim contention is exit 1 — test against that.)
- Re-claim by the same actor → exit 0, idempotent, unchanged.
- `assignee` reads the actor name (`Cyclops`), and `BEADS_ACTOR=Storm bd heartbeat <id>` on
  Cyclops's bead → exit 1, `heartbeat <id>: issue already claimed by Cyclops`.
- `bd unclaim` by the holder → exit 0.

The consumer-side workflow already handles a failing claim — atlantis-hud's CLAUDE.md: "If the
claim fails, another agent won it: pick a different bead." That instruction was dead code while all
actors were one; this bead makes it live. No skill or agent-prompt change is needed for the
implementer's reaction.

All code changes live in the **cerebro submodule** (`rmstdope/cerebro`, mounted at
`.claude/cerebro`), plus one submodule-bump commit in atlantis-hud.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

All paths below are inside the submodule checkout, i.e. `.claude/cerebro/` from the consumer root.

**1. `scripts/run-implementer`** — after the roster validation succeeds (the `if [[ -z "$on_roster" ]]`
block ends at the `exit 2`; the `exec claude \` sits at the bottom of the file), add immediately
before the `exec`:

```bash
# Every bd call in this session acts as this implementer, not as the machine's git identity.
# Distinct actors are what make a second claim on a held bead fail instead of aliasing into the
# first (bd's --actor default chain: $BEADS_ACTOR, git user.name, $USER).
export BEADS_ACTOR="$on_roster"
```

`$on_roster`, not `$name`: it is the canonical spelling from the ROSTER array, so a future
looser-matching change can never leak a miscased actor. The `--roster` early-exit branch is above
this and unaffected. `exec` preserves the environment, and every `Bash` tool subshell inside the
claude session inherits it — nothing else needs to carry the name.

**2. The four role launchers** — same one-line export, hard-coded to the session's fixed name,
immediately before each `exec claude`:

- `scripts/run-planner` (execs with `--name Xavier`) → `export BEADS_ACTOR="Xavier"`
- `scripts/run-orchestrator` (`--name Cerebro`, exec at line 31) → `export BEADS_ACTOR="Cerebro"`
- `scripts/run-user-feedback` (`--name Moira`, exec at line 23) → `export BEADS_ACTOR="Moira"`
- `scripts/run-psylocke` (`--name Psylocke`, exec at line 24) → `export BEADS_ACTOR="Psylocke"`

These roles never claim, but their bd writes (priorities, labels, closes, reopens) enter the audit
trail, and an audit line reading `Xavier` instead of the navigator's own name is the difference
between "an agent did this" and "the human did this". A bead claimed by hand in the navigator's own
shell keeps reading `Henrik Kurelid`, which is now a meaningful signal rather than the only value.

**3. `tests/launchers.sh`** — new file, the submodule's first shell test (there is no test harness
for scripts today; the only suite is ERT for the elisp, run per `CLAUDE.md`). Plain bash, no
framework, `set -euo pipefail`, exit non-zero on first failure, runnable from the submodule root as
`bash tests/launchers.sh`. It must not start a real session: put a stub `claude` executable first on
`PATH` in a temp dir —

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# stub claude: prove what environment and args the launcher hands over
printf 'BEADS_ACTOR=%s\n' "${BEADS_ACTOR:-<unset>}"
printf 'ARG:%s\n' "$@"
```

— then assert:

- `run-implementer Cyclops` output contains `BEADS_ACTOR=Cyclops`;
- `run-implementer storm` still exits 2 and mentions `Storm` (the existing miscased-name message —
  pins that the export did not move above validation);
- `run-implementer --roster` prints exactly the fourteen names and never reaches the stub
  (unchanged behaviour);
- each of the four role launchers' output contains its fixed `BEADS_ACTOR=<Name>`;
- `run-implementer Cyclops` output does **not** contain `BEADS_ACTOR=<unset>`.

**4. `agents/orchestrator.md`** — the claims-sweep prose that this fix falsifies, lines 295-305:
"**But the assignee name is not proof of who holds a claim…** Every claim made from this machine is
stamped with the local git identity … `assignee: Henrik Kurelid` can mean the …". Rewrite that
paragraph to the new truth: a claim from a launched session is stamped with the agent's roster
name; `assignee: Henrik Kurelid` (or any non-roster name) now specifically means a claim made by
hand outside a launched session — still check the lease before touching it, since a claim from
before this change, or from a stale session started off the old launchers, predates the naming.
Keep the lease-first rule at lines 305, 330 and 434 intact — it stays correct and is the guard for
exactly those legacy claims. Check the sweep summary at lines 662-665 for the same stale claim
("the assignee name alone does…") and align its wording.

**5. Consumer bump in atlantis-hud** — after the cerebro PR merges: update the submodule pointer
and commit `feat(ah-rnz): per-agent bd actor identity in the launchers` (precedent: commit
`be6f8fa` / PR #234 for the shape of a bump PR). No atlantis-hud source files change; CLAUDE.md's
"If the claim fails, another agent won it" already describes the new behaviour.

## Increments

TDD here is the shell test playing RED first; there is no other harness for bash in this repo.

1. **The test exists and fails.** Write `tests/launchers.sh` complete (all assertions above). Run
   it: the `--roster` and miscased-name assertions pass (existing behaviour), every `BEADS_ACTOR=`
   assertion fails — that is RED, and it proves the stub harness itself works.
2. **run-implementer exports the actor.** Add the export (file 1). The Cyclops assertions go green.
3. **The role launchers export theirs.** Add the four exports (file 2). The suite is fully green.
4. **The orchestrator prose tells the new truth.** Rewrite `agents/orchestrator.md` per file 4. No
   test pins prose; the check is reading the diff against the paragraph quoted above.
5. **PR against `rmstdope/cerebro`**, reviewed and merged per that repo's flow (it has no CI — say
   in the PR body that `bash tests/launchers.sh` and the ERT suite were run locally, with output).
   Then the bump PR in atlantis-hud (file 5), which runs atlantis-hud's normal CI.

## The test plan

- `bash tests/launchers.sh` — the new suite, green after increment 3.
- `emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit` — the existing 63+ ERT
  tests, which must stay green untouched (nothing in `cerebro.el` changes; `cerebro--roster` shells
  `run-implementer --roster`, whose behaviour the shell test pins as unchanged).
- Live validation, after the bump lands, from the consumer root:
  `BEADS_ACTOR=Storm bd update <some-claimed-bead> --claim` → exit 1 naming the holder. (Or repeat
  the scratch-bead experiment from Context verbatim.)

## User-facing decisions

None. This is fleet tooling; nothing a player of Atlantis HUD sees changes. The navigator set the
priority (P0, 2026-08-15) and chose nothing else because there was nothing visible to choose.

## Out of scope

- Any change to bd itself, to claim semantics, or to lease TTLs — the existing contention behaviour
  (verified above) is exactly what is wanted once actors differ.
- The Emacs fleet view and `cerebro.el` — no elisp changes; the view launches through
  `run-implementer` and inherits the fix.
- Retro-fixing beads claimed under `Henrik Kurelid` before the rollout (see Known traps for the
  rollout order instead).
- Any consumer-side skill or agent-prompt wording beyond `agents/orchestrator.md` — the "claim
  failed, pick another bead" instruction already exists and needs no edit.
- CI for the cerebro repo. Worth having some day; not this bead.

## Validation

```bash
# in the cerebro submodule checkout
bash tests/launchers.sh
emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
```

Then the live claim-contention check under *The test plan*. Human check (Psylocke: this bead is
tooling — mark it not-needed for app verification): none required beyond the fleet running
normally; the visible sign of success is `bd list --status in_progress` showing roster names as
assignees.

## Known traps

- **This is a submodule bead: two PRs, two repos, one order.** The code PR goes to
  `rmstdope/cerebro`. **Never branch inside `.claude/cerebro` itself** — that checkout is shared by
  every session on this machine exactly like the main atlantis-hud checkout, and moving its HEAD
  breaks the launchers for all of them. Work in a clone of your own instead:
  `git clone https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro.git /tmp/ah-rnz-cerebro && cd /tmp/ah-rnz-cerebro
  && git checkout -b ah-rnz-actor-identity`. Not under `.claude/worktrees/` — the prune sweep walks
  that directory and a foreign clone there is something for it to trip over. Only after the cerebro
  PR merges does the atlantis-hud bump PR make sense: from a normal atlantis-hud worktree,
  `git -C .claude/cerebro fetch origin && git -C .claude/cerebro checkout origin/main`, commit the
  pointer, PR. Follow the shape of cerebro PR #7 / atlantis-hud PR #234.
- **In-flight claims at rollout.** A bead claimed under `Henrik Kurelid` before the change cannot
  be heartbeated by a session whose actor is now `Cyclops` — the heartbeat fails exit 1 as "already
  claimed by Henrik Kurelid". Land the bump when no bead is `in_progress`
  (`bd list --status in_progress --json` must be empty), or have the navigator `bd unclaim` the
  stragglers first. Running sessions keep their old identity until restarted; the fleet view
  restarts implementers between beads, so one bead-cycle after the bump the fleet is clean.
- **Claim contention is exit 1, not exit 13.** Exit 13 is the `--if-assignee`/`--if-status` guard
  code. Any test or script written against 13 for a failed claim will pass on entirely the wrong
  outcomes. (The bead description itself gets this wrong; the Context section carries the verified
  behaviour.)
- **The export must sit below the `--roster` branch and the validation** in `run-implementer` —
  above them it would be harmless today but would couple `--roster` (which `cerebro--roster` in the
  fleet view shells on every refresh) to an env mutation nothing wants.
- **Do not touch `--name`.** Liveness of interactive agents is inferred by scanning process args
  for `--name <Name>` (`emacs/cerebro.el`, `cerebro--system-args` consumers); `BEADS_ACTOR` is
  additional, not a replacement.
- **Emacs backup files (`*.el~`, `*.sh~`) are committed in the cerebro repo** — never edit them,
  and do not "clean them up" in this PR.
