The skill must state the cost plainly rather than let each agent rediscover it: expect BEHIND on most merges, budget a rebase plus a full CI cycle per review round, and never treat the rebase as optional. Revisit if the agent count grows past three or so.

title: Protect main so red or stale work cannot merge
description:
gh api reports main is not protected: no ruleset, no required checks, and allow_auto_merge is false. So 'CI must be green' would be enforced only by an agent reading gh pr checks correctly - and every known misreading (a pending check taken as passed, a queued job ignored, a green-but-stale branch) lands straight on main with no backstop. This is the single largest false-green lever in the harness.

A ruleset on main requires the CI job names with branches-up-to-date, auto-merge is enabled, and the agent's merge step becomes gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch --auto: GitHub then owns waiting, ordering and staleness, and the agent's attempt budget becomes a give-up rule rather than a merge-permission rule.

The navigator is a bypass actor. This is a settings change on a live repository and needs the navigator to make it or to approve the exact gh api calls.
acceptance_criteria:
A ruleset on main requires the CI job names and branches to be up to date.
Auto-merge is enabled on the repository.
The navigator is a bypass actor; agent PRs are not exempt.
A deliberately red PR cannot be merged by the documented agent command.
notes: Amended after review with the navigator: a bypass actor was added (RepositoryRole 5, admin, bypass_mode always). Verified by probe - a direct push to main is now permitted with a '10 of 10 required status checks are expected' warning rather than declined. The trade is explicit: agents authenticate with the navigator's token and hold admin, so they inherit the bypass. The ruleset therefore stops accidents (red or stale merges through the PR path, force-pushes, branch deletion) but is not a hard guarantee against an agent that merges deliberately. That guarantee, if wanted later, needs a separate identity for agents.
close_reason: Ruleset 20771276 active on main: 10 required checks, strict up-to-date, no bypass; auto-merge enabled. Verified by a rejected direct push.

title: One cargo build directory, and a disk preflight
description:
There is no .cargo/config.toml, so every git worktree builds its own target tree: 10G + 2.7G + 5.8G for one repository, on a disk that was at 100% capacity with 2.0 GiB free when this was found. Each further implementation agent adds another 3-6 GB, and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets is the biggest of them.

The failure mode is an ENOSPC part-way through a build, which surfaces as a strange linker or codegen error that an agent will try to fix in code.

A committed .cargo/config.toml points every worktree at one shared build directory outside the repo. The per-worktree target trees then become dead weight and can be removed. An implementation agent refuses to start a bead when free space is under a threshold, rather than discovering it mid-build.
acceptance_criteria:
A committed .cargo/config.toml sets a shared build.target-dir outside the repository.
The obsolete per-worktree target trees are removed and the space is measurably reclaimed.
The implement skill refuses to create a worktree below a stated free-space threshold, naming the real cause.

title: Per-agent ports for the smoke and PWA suites
description:
playwright.config.ts pins 4173/4174 and playwright.pwa.config.ts pins 4175. Concurrent agents collide.

The PWA config is the dangerous one: its preview command has no --strictPort, so a second agent's Vite quietly falls back to 4176 while Playwright's readiness probe hits 4175 and finds the FIRST agent's server. Every PWA test then passes against someone else's bundle. The smoke config is safe only by luck, because it does pass --strictPort.

Both configs take a port base from an env var, defaulting to today's numbers so a plain local run is unchanged, and --strictPort is added to the PWA preview so a collision is always loud.
acceptance_criteria:
Both configs derive their ports from an env-provided base, defaulting to 4173/4174/4175.
The PWA preview command passes --strictPort.
Port resolution is a pure function with tests under the tooling vitest config.
Two agents run test:smoke and test:pwa simultaneously and pass against their own bundles; breaking one worktree's source reddens only that agent's run.

title: Export gate stands aside off main
description:
scripts/beadsExportGate.ts writes the whole bead database into .beads/issues.jsonl on every branch it runs on. Two agents' PRs therefore carry complete backlog snapshots taken at different moments, and whichever merges last silently reverts every close, claim, label and plan recorded in between. Git usually will not even conflict, because each side rewrote a different subset of the one-line-per-bead file.

The gate becomes a main-only obligation: on any other branch it stands aside, exactly as it already does when bd is missing or node_modules are absent. main is refreshed by the planner's own pushes and by a post-merge refresh.

This is the highest-probability silent-wrong-result in the harness, and it gets worse once plans live in the design field.
acceptance_criteria:
runGate proceeds without exporting when the current branch is not main.
The existing stand-aside idiom and its tests are followed rather than a new mechanism.
Two branches, each pushed after a bead change and merged in turn, leave the first branch's bead state intact - demonstrated, not assumed.

title: Planner and implementer agent harness
description:
A planning session turns unplanned beads into fully specified ones and owns every UI decision with the navigator; one or more implementation sessions pick up a planned bead, implement it under TDD, get it reviewed by Copilot, merged, and loop.

The split only works if the plan is a real contract and if the agents cannot corrupt each other. A stress test against this repository found five ways the obvious design breaks or silently produces wrong results; the infrastructure children below are those fixes, and they must land before more than one implementation agent runs.

Full design, including the twenty decisions taken with the navigator, is in the children's plans and in the harness skills themselves.
acceptance_criteria:
One planner session and one implementer session carry a real bead from unplanned to merged, with no navigator action beyond the UI discussion during planning.
Two agents can run the smoke and PWA suites at once without testing each other's bundles.
Concurrent PRs no longer overwrite each other's bead state.
close_reason: All 11 children delivered; validated by a live trial on 2026-08-13 in which Cyclops took ah-5jm from claim to merge unattended under scripts/run-implementer

title: Stop agents colliding on a bead someone already claimed
description:
## Summary

Two agents keep starting work on the same bead. The cause is not carelessness — it is that a claim
looks abandoned within minutes of being taken.

`bd update <id> --claim` takes a **lease** with a short TTL, kept alive only by `bd heartbeat`.
Neither `CLAUDE.md` nor the `beads-workflow` skill mentions `bd heartbeat` at all, so no agent here
has ever sent one. A work cycle in this repo — RED, GREEN, REFACTOR, a full local gate, CI — runs an
hour or more against a TTL of roughly five minutes.

Observed, on a bead an agent had claimed ten minutes earlier and was demonstrably still working
(it had already wired a dependency from it):

```
◐ ah-xde · Remove the Classic map theme   [P2 · IN_PROGRESS]
Lease: expires in 1 min (heartbeat 3 mins ago)
```

`bd reclaim` is the reaper: it finds in_progress issues whose lease expired, **clears the assignee
and sets them back to open** so another worker can claim them. `bd update --force` documents itself
as being for "abandoned claims — crashed agent, expired lease". With nobody heartbeating, every live
claim in this repository matches that description exactly.

Three contributing findings:

- **The selection window.** The loop claims before branching, but exploration and planning happen
  first — one bead was planned for ten minutes before it was claimed. Selected-but-unclaimed work is
  invisible to every other agent.
- **Worktrees are not the problem.** All three worktrees resolve to the same Dolt database, so a
  claim is visible locally the moment it is written.
- **Cross-machine is.** Leases are node-local and write no Dolt commit; only status and assignee
  commit, and those travel only on `bd dolt push`/`bd dolt pull`. The skill says to push at session
  end, so a claim can stay invisible to another machine for an entire session.

`claim.ttl` is not a documented config key — `bd config get claim.ttl` reports "not set", and the
skill already records that `bd config set` accepts unknown keys silently — so lengthening the TTL is
not a reliable lever. The fix belongs in the instructions.

## Scope

Update `.claude/skills/beads-workflow/SKILL.md` and `CLAUDE.md` (the symlink to
`.github/copilot-instructions.md`) with four rules, agreed with the navigator:

1. **Claim first.** `bd update <id> --claim` is the first action after choosing a bead — before
   exploring, planning or asking questions, not merely before branching. A failed claim means
   somebody else won; pick another bead.
2. **Heartbeat while working.** `bd heartbeat <id>` at every phase gate and before any long wait (a
   full smoke run, a CI watch). Heartbeats write no Dolt commit and no history, so the cadence is
   free.
3. **Never take over a claim unasked.** `in_progress` with an assignee is authoritative whatever the
   lease says. No `bd reclaim`, no `bd update --force`, no reassignment over a live claim without
   the navigator saying so — an expired lease here means "nobody heartbeated", not "the worker
   died".
4. **Push the claim immediately.** `bd dolt push` right after claiming, not only at session end, so
   another machine can see it. Keep the session-end push as well.

Record the lease behaviour itself in the skill's Traps section, so an agent that meets a stale lease
recognises it rather than reasoning from `--force`'s help text.

## Out of scope

- Changing `claim.ttl` or any beads configuration; the key is not part of the documented surface.
- A supervisor process running `bd reclaim` on a timer. That is the upstream design for dead-worker
  recovery, and it is exactly what must not run here while nothing heartbeats.

## Validation

- `bd heartbeat <id>` on a bead this session holds, confirming the lease moves forward — the one
  claim in the four rules that has never actually been exercised here.
- Re-read both documents end to end: the daily loop, the checklist and CLAUDE.md's work-package
  rules must agree with each other, since all three currently describe claiming.
- No code changes, so the gate is `pnpm run lint` for the markdown-adjacent tooling only.
acceptance_criteria:
The beads-workflow skill and CLAUDE.md both say to claim before exploring or planning, not merely before branching.
Both say to heartbeat during long work, naming bd heartbeat.
Both forbid bd reclaim, bd update --force and reassignment over a live claim without the navigator's approval.
Both say to bd dolt push straight after claiming, in addition to at session end.
The skill's Traps section explains the lease TTL and why an expired lease here does not mean an abandoned worker.

title: implement-bead: check mergeStateStatus before polling gh pr checks after a force-push
description:
An implementer waiting for CI after a rebase/force-push can waste a wait cycle polling , whose state can be stale, when the real problem is that the branch is CONFLICTING against main and GitHub never ran (or won't meaningfully complete) a fresh check run against that head.

Observed on ah-k6i.5 (PR #285, 2026-08-15): after rebasing and force-pushing, `gh pr view --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus` already showed `DIRTY`/`CONFLICTING`, but the implementer went straight into the *Waiting, without ending your run* CI-poll loop from `implement-bead` anyway, reading stale/cached check state. The navigator had to interrupt and point out the conflict. A second rebase then surfaced a real conflict against a sibling bead's PR (ah-k6i.3) that had also touched AppShell.tsx, which was resolved correctly — but the wasted poll cycle itself was never caught by the process.
design: Likely lands in `.claude/skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md`'s *Merging* section, right where it already says to expect `BEHIND` on most merges. Add a sentence: check mergeable/mergeStateStatus is not CONFLICTING/DIRTY before waiting on checks; a conflicted head's check state may be stale rather than a real signal to wait on.
acceptance_criteria: `implement-bead`'s *Merging* section (or *Waiting, without ending your run*) is updated so that, after any push that could have raced main (a rebase, an `update-branch` call), the implementer checks `gh pr view --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus` for `CONFLICTING`/`DIRTY` BEFORE entering the CI-poll loop — and if conflicting, resolves the conflict (or re-syncs) first rather than polling checks. The change is a documentation/skill edit, not application code.
notes: Filed from a navigator conversation during ah-k6i.5's implementation (Cyclops), not from Bishop's sweep — this is a process gap in the implementer skill itself, not a codebase smell.

title: The map on screen is derived from the core's known map, not rebuilt in TypeScript
description: Third slice of ah-u4e. gameMemory's outcomes (rememberTurn, readMemory, restoreLatestTurn, mergeTurn) carry the core-built known map alongside the remembered regions; buildHexMapModel becomes a synchronous conversion of that model into HexNodes (labels, knowledge word, ages, unit counts) with every precedence rule deleted from hexMapModel.ts; the smoke suite and the map tests must not change what they see.

title: The known map crosses the core boundary as one command, for both shells
description: Second slice of ah-u4e. build_known_map(raw_report, remembered_json) exposed like plan_route/export_map: core-tauri command + main.rs wrapper + native SWEEP row, core-wasm function, browser-core module + web adapter, core-client CoreAdapter/CoreClient/createTauriAdapter with a camelCase DTO. No caller yet beyond a parity/round-trip test.
design:
## Context

Second slice of **ah-u4e**, on **ah-u4e.1** (planned; blocks this — read its plan: it creates
`crates/core/src/known_map.rs` with `resolve_known_map(current: &ParsedReport, remembered:
&[RememberedRegion]) -> KnownMap`, `KnownMap { hexes: Vec<KnownMapHex>, current_turn }`,
`KnownMapHex { coordinate, terrain, province, knowledge: Current|Stale|Named, last_seen_turn,
region: Option<ReportRegion> }`, all `serde(rename_all = "camelCase")`). This slice carries that
resolution across the core boundary as **one command, `known_map`**, in exactly the shape
`export_map`/`plan_route` already cross it — the pure "arguments in, JSON out" shape with no
storage — so ah-u4e.3 can replace `buildHexMapModel`'s rules with a call. **No caller in the shell
yet**; the proof is a round trip in the tests of every layer plus the native sweep row.

The parse choice matters for what the hexes show: the shell parses *classified* when the ruleset is
to hand (`reportParser`, ah-k6i.5) so units carry exact men counts; the command therefore takes an
optional `ruleset_json` and uses `cache.classified_when_possible` (`crates/core/src/cache.rs:93-101`)
— the pattern `command_merge_report` uses (`core-tauri/src/lib.rs:985-993`) and `validate_orders`
crosses with `Option<String>` (`main.rs:371-379`, `core-wasm/src/lib.rs:720-724`, `core-client`
`rulesetJson: string | null` :874-880). Line numbers against `origin/main` after #284.

## Files to change, and what to reuse (one command, five layers — the `export_map` trail)

### `crates/core/src/known_map.rs` (from .1) — add the text entry beside the pure one

```rust
/// The boundary's entry: parses RAW-REPORT (classified when RULESET-JSON is given), reads the
/// remembered regions from their JSON, and resolves. Errors name what could not be read.
pub fn known_map_json(cache: &mut ReportCache, raw_report: &str, ruleset_json: Option<&str>, remembered_json: &str) -> Result<KnownMap, String>
```
`remembered_json` is deserialised as `Vec<RememberedRegion>` with the message
`remembered regions could not be read: {error}` (`movement/request.rs:88-90`'s wording).

### `crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs` — beside `command_export_map` (:1119-1132)

`pub fn command_known_map(raw_report: &str, ruleset_json: Option<&str>, remembered_json: &str) -> Result<KnownMap, String>`
via `cache::with_global`. Doc: the desktop twin of the wasm binding, same core entry, "so the two
shells cannot drift" — the sentence every twin here carries.

### `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs` — beside `export_map` (:228-238) and in `generate_handler!` (:485-516)

```rust
#[tauri::command(rename_all = "snake_case")]
fn known_map(raw_report: String, ruleset_json: Option<String>, remembered_json: String) -> Result<KnownMap, String> {
    atlantis_hud_core_tauri::command_known_map(&raw_report, ruleset_json.as_deref(), &remembered_json)
}
```
(`KnownMap` is `Serialize`, camelCase — no DTO needed; the same cfg block as its neighbours.) Add
`known_map,` to the handler list **and** a `SWEEP` row in `tests/native/binding.spec.ts` (after
`export_map`, :120-…): `args: () => ({ raw_report: REPORT, ruleset_json: null, remembered_json: "[]" })`
— the lockstep (ah-ga6, if merged, runs locally: `pnpm run test:tooling`).

### `crates/core-wasm/src/lib.rs` — beside `export_map_state` (:626-643)

`pub fn known_map_state(raw_report: String, ruleset_json: Option<String>, remembered_json: String) -> Result<JsValue, JsValue>`
→ `to_js(&known_map)`. (After ah-350 this crate carries only pure functions; this is one.)

### `packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.ts` — the module type (:44) and the adapter (:619-623)

`known_map_state(rawReport: string, rulesetJson: string | null, rememberedJson: string): unknown;`
and `knownMap(rawReport, rulesetJson, rememberedJson) { return wasm.known_map_state(...) }` —
"straight through", as `exportMap`'s comment says.

### `packages/core-client/src/index.ts`

- Wire types: `KnownMapDto` = `{ hexes: KnownMapHexDto[]; currentTurn: number | null }`,
  `KnownMapHexDto = { coordinate: Coordinate; terrain: string; province: string; knowledge: "current" | "stale" | "named"; lastSeenTurn: number | null; region: ReportRegion | null }`
  — camelCase from serde on both transports, so no `normalize*` beyond the `ReportRegion` one the
  client already applies to regions (find how `loadRegionSightings` normalises `RememberedRegion.region`
  and reuse that function on each `region`).
- `CoreAdapter` (:899-905 neighbourhood): `knownMap(rawReport: string, rulesetJson: string | null, rememberedJson: string): Promise<unknown> | unknown;`
- `CoreClient` (:1087): `knownMap(rawReport: string, rulesetJson: string | null, remembered: RememberedRegion[]): Promise<KnownMap>;` — the client stringifies `remembered` (as `planRoute`'s callers do with `rememberedJson`; check whether the client or the shell stringifies today — follow `exportMap` (:2022-2023), where the client stringifies the request).
- `createCoreClient` (:2022 neighbourhood): `async knownMap(...) { const raw = await adapter.knownMap(rawReport, rulesetJson, JSON.stringify(remembered)); return normalizeKnownMap(raw); }`.
- `createTauriAdapter` (:2459-2465): `invoke<KnownMapDto>("known_map", { raw_report, ruleset_json, remembered_json })`.
- Exported types `KnownMap`, `KnownMapHex`, `HexKnowledge` (the last exists in `hexMapModel.ts:16`;
  ah-u4e.3 will re-point it — here define it in core-client and leave shared's alone).

### Tests

- Rust: `crates/core/tests/known_map.rs` (from .1) gains `known_map_json_reads_its_arguments` (a
  report, `null` ruleset, `"[]"`) and `rejects_unreadable_remembered_json` (message prefix).
  core-tauri: if it has a test file per command (`git ls-tree origin/main crates/core-tauri/tests`),
  one round-trip; core-wasm: nothing beyond the build (its host tests are DTO-only).
- `packages/core-client/src/index.test.ts`: the tauri contract case (as ah-350 leaves it) gains
  `knownMap` — invoke called with the three snake_case keys, `null` passing through as `null`, and
  the answer's regions normalised like `loadRegionSightings`'s.
- `packages/browser-core` tests: the adapter forwards to `wasm.known_map_state` (their existing
  pattern for `exportMap`).
- `tests/native/binding.spec.ts`: the `SWEEP` row (above).

## Increments

1. RED: the two Rust `known_map.rs` tests. GREEN: `known_map_json` + `command_known_map`.
2. `main.rs` wrapper + handler + `SWEEP` row; `known_map_state`; `cargo build -p
   atlantis-hud-core-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` and `cargo check --workspace
   --features desktop-runtime` (or whatever `apps/desktop` builds with — read its `Cargo.toml`;
   the local gate cfgs the wrappers out, ah-ga6's Context).
3. RED: core-client and browser-core tests. GREEN: the four TypeScript sites. `pnpm run typecheck`.
4. `pnpm run check`; PR `feat(ah-u4e.2): the known map crosses the core boundary as one command`;
   `@copilot`; CI — watch `native` (the sweep row) and `wasm`; squash. Close the bead, not the epic.

## The test plan

- Rust workspace tests + clippy + fmt; the wasm target build; core-client, browser-core suites;
  `pnpm run test:tooling` (the lockstep, if ah-ga6 has merged); `pnpm run check`; CI `native` green
  with `known_map` in the sweep.

## User-facing decisions

None — no caller yet. Navigator: P2 at triage (2026-08-15).

## Out of scope

- Any use of the command by the shell (ah-u4e.3).
- The IndexedDB store: this command has no persistence, so `webCoreAdapter` has no store twin.
- Generating the boundary (ah-wxk).

## Validation

```bash
cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace
cargo build -p atlantis-hud-core-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown
pnpm run typecheck && pnpm --filter @atlantis/core-client test && pnpm --filter @atlantis/browser-core test
pnpm run test:tooling && pnpm run check
```

Human check: none; Psylocke marks not-needed.

## Known traps

- **Register and sweep in the same commit** (`main.rs` + `binding.spec.ts`) — the five-times slip
  ah-ga6 exists for; if ah-ga6 has merged, `pnpm run test:tooling` catches it locally.
- **`Option<String>` crosses Tauri as `null` and wasm as `undefined`/`null`** — the client passes
  `null`, never `""`, and the Rust side treats `None` as "parse full" (`classified_when_possible`).
- **The classified cache key** — `cache.classified` is keyed on `(raw, ruleset)`; passing the same
  ruleset text the shell uses elsewhere keeps the parse shared; do not re-serialise the ruleset.
- **`ReportRegion` normalisation on the TS side** — the wire regions carry whatever casing the
  serde attributes give (`camelCase` here); reuse the existing normaliser and its test rather than
  writing a second.
- **Do not add a wasm32 stub pair** — this is a pure function present on both targets (ah-350's
  point).

title: One resolver in core decides what every remembered sighting contributes to the known map
description: First slice of ah-u4e. The precedence rules for building the accumulated map - a current-report hex beats a stored sighting, a visited hex beats one merely named by an exit, namings oldest-first with the first naming in a turn winning, units only from a current-turn sighting (the current report or a same-turn ally) - are written once in Rust, in a resolver that both MapKnowledge (planner/risk) and, from ah-u4e.2, the shell's display model are built from. Fixes today's disagreement (Rust drops a same-turn ally's units, the screen shows them). Tests pin every rule.
design:
## Context

First slice of **ah-u4e** (epic, three children, this first). The map accumulated across turns is
built twice from the same stored sightings: in Rust for the planner and the risk assessment
(`crates/core/src/movement/graph.rs`, `MapKnowledge::from_remembered` :253-274, `remember`
:276-307, `rebuild_exits` :309-336) and in TypeScript for the screen
(`packages/shared/src/hexMapModel.ts`, `buildHexMapModel` :249-361, `withAlliesUnits` :156-174).
Every precedence rule is re-derived by hand on the TS side, and two navigator-reported bugs a day
apart were each a rule Rust carried and TS lacked (ah-ctf: exit-only neighbours from earlier turns;
ah-o86: units from older sightings shown as current). They still disagree today: Rust
`from_remembered` drops units from *every* remembered region, including a same-turn ally sighting,
so `assess_hex` reads "Nobody else is here." (`movement/risk.rs:208`) where the map shows the ally's
units (`hexMapModel.ts:302-306`).

This slice writes the rules **once, in core**: a `known_map` module whose `resolve_known_map(current,
remembered)` decides, for every hex the faction knows, what it is (current / stale / merely named),
when it was last seen, and which region description — with which units — it contributes; `MapKnowledge`
is then *derived* from that resolution (adjacency and the planning-only rule about structures stay
its own). ah-u4e.2 exposes the resolution over the boundary; ah-u4e.3 makes the screen consume it and
deletes the TS rules. **The one behaviour change** here is the disagreement itself: with a same-turn
ally sighting, the planner and the risk text now see the ally's units, as the map already does —
a bug fix in the direction of consistency, not a design choice.

Line numbers against atlantis-hud `origin/main` after #284.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### New: `crates/core/src/known_map.rs` (`pub mod known_map;` in `lib.rs:3-6`, alphabetical)

```rust
use crate::movement::graph::RememberedRegion;
use crate::report::model::{Coordinate, Exit, ParsedReport, ReportRegion};

/// How much can be trusted about a hex on the accumulated map - the same three words the screen
/// uses (`hexMapModel.ts` `HexKnowledge`), owned here now.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub enum HexKnowledge { Current, Stale, Named }

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct KnownMapHex {
    pub coordinate: Coordinate,
    pub terrain: String,
    pub province: String,
    pub knowledge: HexKnowledge,
    /// The turn this description dates from: the current turn, the sighting's turn, or the turn of
    /// the exit that named it. `None` only when the current report itself carries no turn number.
    pub last_seen_turn: Option<u32>,
    /// The region as it may be shown or planned over: the current report's block (plus a same-turn
    /// ally's extra units, marked foreign); a same-turn ally sighting as stored; an older sighting
    /// with its units dropped. `None` for a hex merely named by an exit.
    pub region: Option<ReportRegion>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct KnownMap {
    /// Sorted by z, then y, then x - the screen's order (`hexMapModel.ts:333-341`).
    pub hexes: Vec<KnownMapHex>,
    pub current_turn: Option<u32>,
}

/// Everything the faction knows, resolved once. See the module doc for the precedence rules.
#[must_use]
pub fn resolve_known_map(current: &ParsedReport, remembered: &[RememberedRegion]) -> KnownMap;
```

The rules, in the order they are applied (weakest first, each overwriting the last), ported from
`buildHexMapModel` and `MapKnowledge::remember` — write them in the module doc as a numbered list:

1. **Namings from memory** (`hexMapModel.ts:257-273`): remembered regions' exits, oldest
   `last_seen_turn` first (stable sort), and within one turn the *first* naming of a hex wins; each
   yields a `Named` hex with the exit's terrain/province and `last_seen_turn` = that sighting's turn.
2. **Namings from the current report** (:275-288): the current report's exits, first naming wins,
   `last_seen_turn` = current turn; they overwrite memory's namings.
3. **Stored sightings** (:290-317): each remembered region overwrites a `Named` hex (never a visited
   one — one sighting per coordinate is what storage hands back, so the "existing is not named"
   guard is a defence, keep it): `Current` with its units when `last_seen_turn == current_turn`
   (a same-turn ally sighting), else `Stale` with `units` emptied. Terrain/province/exits from the
   region.
4. **The current report's regions** (:319-328): `Current`, `last_seen_turn` = current turn, region =
   the block **plus** a same-turn stored sighting's units it does not name, appended with `own =
   false` (`withAlliesUnits`, :156-174 — port the "additive only, this turn only" rule and its
   comment).

`Coordinate` ordering for the final sort: `(z, y, x)`; `regionId` is not stored (the screen derives
it from the coordinate as today, `regionIdOf`).

### `crates/core/src/movement/graph.rs`

- `MapKnowledge::from_remembered` (:253-274) becomes: `let known = resolve_known_map(current,
  remembered); Self::from_known_map(&known)`.
- New `pub fn from_known_map(known: &KnownMap) -> Self`: for every hex, a `KnownHex` with
  `visited = knowledge != Named`; `roads` from the region's `Road *` structures (as `remember` does,
  :283-288); **`structures` only when `Current`** — planning's own rule, keep the comment at
  :289-296 ("a fleet can sail away…") but reworded: the resolver decides *who is there*, this
  decides *what planning may count*; `units = region.units` as resolved (which is where the ally
  fix lands); `last_seen_turn` from the hex; then `pending_exits` from every hex's region exits and
  `rebuild_exits()` as today — with one change: `rebuild_exits`'s `or_insert_with` (:321-333) must
  no longer fire for a hex the resolution already placed (it will not, since every named hex is in
  `hexes` already; keep the `or_insert_with` as a defence and say so).
- `remember` (:276-307) is deleted (only `from_remembered` called it; `from_report` :192-251 has its
  own loops — leave `from_report` alone: it is the no-memory path and its rules are the same as
  resolving with `remembered = &[]`; add a test asserting that equivalence, and if it holds, make
  `from_report` call `from_remembered(report, &[])` — a smaller graph.rs).
- `RememberedRegion` (:181-184) stays where it is (the resolver imports it).

### Tests — new `crates/core/tests/known_map.rs` (the `parse_report_full` + `at(x, y)` style of `movement_graph.rs:17-27`)

One test per rule, tiny reports:
- `a_current_report_hex_beats_a_stored_sighting_of_it` — same hex in both; `Current`, the report's
  units, `last_seen_turn` = current.
- `an_older_sighting_is_stale_and_keeps_no_units` — units empty, `Stale`, terrain kept.
- `a_same_turn_ally_sighting_is_current_and_keeps_its_units` — `last_seen_turn == current`; `Current`,
  units present.
- `an_allys_units_join_the_current_hex_marked_foreign` — same-turn stored sighting of a hex the
  report describes: the report's units first, the extra ones appended with `own == false`; a unit
  named by both appears once.
- `an_older_naming_is_overwritten_by_a_newer_one_and_the_first_in_a_turn_wins` — two remembered
  regions of different turns naming the same hex with different terrain; and two of the same turn.
- `the_current_reports_naming_wins_over_memorys` and `a_visited_hex_beats_one_merely_named`.
- `hexes_come_out_sorted_by_level_then_row_then_column`.
- In `movement_graph.rs`: `the_planner_sees_a_same_turn_allys_units` — `from_remembered` with a
  same-turn ally sighting: `hex(...).units` non-empty (today's behaviour would fail this);
  `a_stale_sighting_contributes_roads_but_no_structures_to_planning`; the existing
  `remembered_regions_join_the_map_up_where_one_report_cannot` (:276-320) unchanged and green.
- In `movement_risk.rs` tests: find the case behind "Nobody else is here." and add its mirror — a
  same-turn ally-seen hex names the units instead. (Read `assess_hex`'s callers first; if
  `assess_hex` reads `KnownHex.units`, the new `from_remembered` already changes it.)

### Docs

`crates/core/src/known_map.rs` module doc is the specification; `hexMapModel.ts:249-256`'s doc
comment gets one line pointing at it as the source of the rules ("ported to core by ah-u4e.1; this
file's copy is deleted by ah-u4e.3").

## Increments

1. RED: `known_map.rs` tests 1-4 (current beats stored; stale drops units; same-turn ally current;
   ally units appended). GREEN: the module with rules 3-4 and a plain namings pass.
2. RED: the naming-precedence and sort tests. GREEN: rules 1-2 exactly as ported.
3. RED: `the_planner_sees_a_same_turn_allys_units` and the stale-structures test in
   `movement_graph.rs`. GREEN: `from_known_map`, `from_remembered` through it, `remember` deleted;
   the `from_report` equivalence test; the risk mirror.
4. `cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test
   --workspace`; `pnpm run check` (the shell is untouched, but `plan_route`/`export_map` outputs
   flow from `MapKnowledge`, and the smoke suite exercises routes); PR `refactor(ah-u4e.1): the
   known map is resolved once in core, and the planner sees a same-turn ally's units`;
   `@copilot`; CI; squash. Close the bead, not the epic.

## The test plan

- `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core` (new `known_map.rs`, `movement_graph.rs`, `movement_risk.rs`,
  `movement_plan.rs` unchanged), the workspace suite, clippy, `pnpm run check`.

## User-facing decisions

None asked. The one visible change — the route planner's risk line for a hex an ally saw this same
turn now names those units instead of "Nobody else is here." — is the resolution of a documented
disagreement in favour of what the map already shows. Navigator: P2 at triage (2026-08-15).

## Out of scope

- The boundary command (ah-u4e.2) and the TS consumer (ah-u4e.3): `hexMapModel.ts` is unchanged here
  except for one doc line.
- Any change to what `plan_route`/`export_map` return beyond the ally-units fix.

## Validation

```bash
cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace
pnpm run check
```

Human check (Psylocke, optional): merge an ally's same-turn report, plan a route through a hex only
the ally saw — the risk text names the ally's units.

## Known traps

- **`Coordinate` ordering**: sort explicitly by `(z, y, x)`; do not rely on `Ord` on `Coordinate`
  unless it is defined that way (check `report/model.rs`).
- **Stable sort for the namings** (`sort_by_key` is stable in Rust) — the "first naming in a turn
  wins" rule depends on the storage order surviving the sort, exactly as `namingsOldestFirst` in TS.
- **`from_report`'s exit-hex creation order differs from the resolver's** (BTreeMap iteration vs
  first-naming) — the equivalence test may fail on a report that names one hex from two regions with
  different terrain (rare, but the fixture reports may contain one); if it does, the resolver's rule
  is the one to keep, and `from_report` delegates to it.
- **The risk suite's wording** — grep for the exact string before editing; other tests may pin it.
- **Rebase risk**: `movement/graph.rs` is stable; `hexMapModel.ts` moves under ah-j3p (no overlap).

title: Cerebro's state, stop flags and worktrees move out of .claude/ into .cerebro/
description:
Cerebro is a harness that happens to drive Claude. Everything it owns currently lives under
`.claude/`, which says the opposite — that the harness is part of Claude and would have to be
rebuilt to run anything else.

**First step: move the files cerebro owns to `.cerebro/`, and leave in `.claude/` only what Claude
itself must find there.**

## The split

| Path | Refs | Whose | Where it goes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.claude/agents-state/` | 30 | cerebro's | **`.cerebro/agents-state/`** — state files and stop flags |
| `.claude/worktrees/` | 34 | cerebro's | **`.cerebro/worktrees/`** — where implementers build |
| `.claude/agents/` | 3 | Claude's | stays — this is Claude Code's discovery path |
| `.claude/skills/` | 2 | Claude's | stays — same |
| `.claude/settings.json` | — | Claude's | stays |
| `.claude/cerebro` | 115 | ? | **see below** |

Nothing in the first two is read by Claude. They are cerebro's own bookkeeping, and they are the
whole of what a second harness would need to reimplement or share.

## The submodule mount is the open question

`.claude/cerebro` is 115 of the 179 references and is neither Claude's nor obviously runtime. A
harness that is not Claude-specific mounting itself inside `.claude/` is exactly the confusion this
bead is trying to end — and moving it is much the largest part of the change: `.gitmodules`, every
documented path in five agent files and three skills, the sync script's `../../..` climb to the
consumer root, and a re-clone for anyone who has it checked out.

Doing it in the same pass is coherent. Deferring it is defensible. Doing it *later* means paying the
documentation cost twice. Worth deciding now rather than discovering it half-way.

## Two dependents that break quietly

**Root detection.** `cerebro--repo-root` finds the consumer root with
`locate-dominating-file default-directory ".claude/cerebro"` — chosen deliberately over
`agents-state`, because the submodule exists from clone time while the state directory is created on
first write. Whatever moves, that anchor has to keep the same property: present in a fresh clone,
before any agent has run.

**The consumer's `.gitignore`.** atlantis-hud carries:

    .claude/*
    !.claude/skills/
    !.claude/agents/
    !.claude/settings.json
    !.claude/cerebro

A new top-level `.cerebro/` is untracked and unignored, so state files and worktrees would start
showing up in `git status` — and in an implementer's `git status --porcelain` check, which
`prune-worktrees.sh` uses to decide whether a worktree is safe to remove. That check reads a clean
tree as "nothing can be lost". This must be ignored in the same change, not afterwards.

## Migration

The rename cannot happen under a running fleet: a live implementer's state file and its worktree
would both move out from under it. Either the fleet is down for the change, or the code reads both
locations for a transition — and the second is more machinery than a harness this young needs.

## For the planner to settle with the navigator

- **Does `.claude/cerebro` move to `.cerebro/harness` (or similar) in this pass, or a later one?**
- **What anchors the root** once `.claude/cerebro` may not be there.
- Whether `agents-state` keeps its name under the new root, now that it holds every agent's state
  rather than the implementers' — `.cerebro/state/` reads better and is one more thing to rename.
- Whether the consumer's `.gitignore` gains `.cerebro/` wholesale, or with exceptions the way
  `.claude/` has.

## Validation

With the fleet stopped: rename, start an implementer, and confirm it claims a bead, writes state to
the new path, builds in the new worktree directory, is stopped by a flag written there, and is
replaced on `done`. Confirm `git status` is clean throughout — nothing from the new directory
appears — and that `prune-worktrees.sh` still finds and sweeps a stale worktree.
design:
## Context

Cerebro is a harness that happens to drive Claude, but everything it owns lives under `.claude/`
— its state files and stop flags (`.claude/agents-state/`, since ah-2n3.1) and the agents'
worktrees (`.claude/worktrees/`) — which says the harness is part of Claude. This bead moves
**cerebro's own bookkeeping** to a top-level **`.cerebro/`** in the consumer and leaves in
`.claude/` only what Claude Code itself must find there: `agents/`, `skills/`, `settings.json`, and
— **by the navigator's decision, deferred** — the submodule mount `.claude/cerebro` itself.

Settled with the navigator (2026-08-15): the **mount stays** at `.claude/cerebro` (it is 115 of
the ~180 references, needs a `.gitmodules` change and a re-clone, and root detection anchors on it —
a later bead can move it, with nothing to migrate but paths); state and stop flags go to
**`.cerebro/state/`** (rejected: `.cerebro/agents-state/` — the "agents-" was there to stand apart
from `implementers/` under `.claude/`, which `.cerebro/` makes redundant); worktrees go to
**`.cerebro/worktrees/`**; the consumer's `.gitignore` ignores **`.cerebro/` wholesale** (rejected:
an exceptions pattern like `.claude/*` — nothing tracked will ever live there). Root detection is
therefore **untouched**: `cerebro--repo-root` (cerebro.el:875-882) and `scripts/consumer-root`
(ah-e0w) both anchor on `.claude/cerebro`, which is present from clone time.

**This is a rename with a fleet-down migration.** A live implementer's state file and worktree
would move out from under it, and git worktrees cannot be `mv`ed (the registry under `.git/worktrees`
records the path — `git worktree move` is the tool). The migration is the navigator's, scripted in
the PR description; the code reads **one** location, no transition period (the bead's own call, and
the right one for a harness this young).

**Where the code lives.** cerebro submodule (`emacs/`, `scripts/`, `tests/`, `agents/`, `skills/`,
`docs/`, `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`), PR 1 to `rmstdope/cerebro`; atlantis-hud PR 2: the bump plus
`.gitignore`, `CLAUDE.md` + `.github/copilot-instructions.md` (byte-identical), `.cargo/config.toml`
(comment), `scripts/cargoTargetDir.ts` + test. Line numbers against cerebro `origin/main`
**`d05694b`** and atlantis-hud `origin/main` after #280; **`git grep -n 'claude/agents-state\|claude/worktrees'`
in each repo is the checklist and must come back empty at the end** (except `docs/retrospectives/`
and `.beads/issues.jsonl` in atlantis-hud, which are history).

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### cerebro — code (three real sites; everything else is prose)

- `emacs/cerebro.el`: `cerebro--state-file-path` (:904) → `".cerebro/state/%s.state.json"`;
  `cerebro--stop-flag-path` (:1188) → `".cerebro/state/%s.stop"`; the header comment (:17), the
  `cerebro--supervise-action` docstring (:613), `cerebro--repo-root`'s docstring (:878 — it still
  anchors on `.claude/cerebro`; say the state directory is now `.cerebro/state`), and
  `cerebro--write-stop-flag`'s docstring (:1942-1944).
- `scripts/agent-state`: `out_dir="$repo_root/.cerebro/state"` (:136) and the head comment (:3).
- `scripts/prune-worktrees.sh`: the `case` at :101 → `"$repo_root"/.cerebro/worktrees/*)`; comments
  at :5, :20, :29 (the `psylocke` exception at :108 is by basename and needs no change).
- `scripts/run-orchestrator:13` comment.

### cerebro — tests

- `emacs/cerebro-test.el:1095` — the stop-flag path expectation → `/repo/.cerebro/state/Cyclops.stop`;
  :555 docstring text.
- `tests/agent-state.sh` — `state_file` (:52), the `mkdir -p` (:190), the `find` (:205), and the
  worktree case (:281-296): fixture worktree at `$tmp/.cerebro/worktrees/ah-f9c`, assert the file
  lands in `$tmp/.cerebro/state/` and `$worktree/.cerebro/state` does not exist.
- `tests/consumer-root.sh:46` — the fixture worktree path → `.cerebro/worktrees/wt` (the resolver's
  answer does not depend on it, but the fixture should mirror the real layout).

### cerebro — prose (search-and-replace, then read each site)

`agents/orchestrator.md` (14 lines: `agents-state` ×12, `worktrees` ×2), `agents/verifier.md`
(worktrees ×15 — Psylocke's persistent worktree becomes `.cerebro/worktrees/psylocke`, :124-131),
`agents/planner.md`, `agents/implementer.md`, `agents/user-feedback.md`, `agents/architect.md`,
`skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md` (×8), `skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md` (×6),
`skills/beads-workflow/SKILL.md` (×3), `docs/agent-workflow.md` (×6), `emacs/README.md` (×2),
`README.md`, `CLAUDE.md` (×2 — and add one Gotcha: `.cerebro/` is the harness's own directory in
the consumer, ignored wholesale; `.claude/` holds only what Claude Code discovers plus the mount).
The `.gitignore` snippet quoted in `agents/orchestrator.md` or elsewhere, if any, shows the new
line.

### atlantis-hud — PR 2

- `.gitignore` (:30-37): keep the `.claude/*` block (the mount and Claude's own dirs are still
  there); rewrite its comment (state is no longer under `.claude/`), and add:
  ```
  # Cerebro's own bookkeeping - agent state files, stop flags and the agents' worktrees. Live
  # machine state, never part of the project (ah-v82).
  .cerebro/
  ```
- `CLAUDE.md` (:54, :56, :74, :88, :187, :322) and `.github/copilot-instructions.md` — same six
  edits; `diff` them afterwards (byte-identical is a rule of that file pair, see #264's PR body).
- `.cargo/config.toml` (:3, :11) — comment only; `target-dir` unchanged (a worktree under
  `.cerebro/worktrees/` is still inside the repository, so the shared build dir still holds).
- `scripts/cargoTargetDir.ts:5` — `AGENT_WORKSPACES = ".cerebro"`; doc comment. Its test
  (`scripts/cargoTargetDir.test.ts`, the `strayWorktrees` table and the temp-repo case at :38-46
  after ah-efj) → `.cerebro/worktrees/…` in the fixture paths; the "sibling merely named after"
  case becomes `.cerebro-old`.
- Bump the submodule pointer to PR 1's merge.
- **PR description = the migration script**, verbatim for the navigator:
  ```bash
  # 1. Fleet down: every implementer done and retired (f on each, wait for dead), Psylocke, Xavier, Cerebro, Moira ended; close the Emacs fleet view.
  # 2. Pull main (this PR merged) and update the submodule:
  git pull && git submodule update --init --recursive
  # 3. Move the bookkeeping:
  mkdir -p .cerebro
  mv .claude/agents-state .cerebro/state
  git worktree list                                   # anything under .claude/worktrees/:
  git worktree move .claude/worktrees/psylocke .cerebro/worktrees/psylocke   # or `git worktree remove --force` and let Psylocke re-create it
  # (repeat for any other live one; a stale one: git worktree remove --force <path>)
  git worktree prune
  rmdir .claude/worktrees 2>/dev/null; rm -rf .claude/implementers          # the pre-ah-2n3.1 directory, if still there
  # 4. Restart the fleet view (loads the new cerebro.el), then start the agents again.
  ```

## Increments

1. RED: `tests/agent-state.sh` (state_file/worktree case on the new paths) and the ERT stop-flag
   test — fail against today's paths. GREEN: `agent-state`, `cerebro.el`'s two paths, and the
   docstrings; `tests/consumer-root.sh` fixture path.
2. `prune-worktrees.sh`; then the prose sweep; `git grep -n 'claude/agents-state\|claude/worktrees'`
   empty in the cerebro tree. Byte-compile, ERT, the four bash suites green. PR 1
   `feat(ah-v82): cerebro's own state, flags and worktrees live under .cerebro/`, `@copilot`, CI,
   squash.
3. atlantis-hud PR 2: `.gitignore`, the CLAUDE.md pair, `.cargo/config.toml` comment,
   `cargoTargetDir.ts` + test (RED on the constant's test first), the bump; `git grep` clean except
   retrospectives and the beads export; **the migration script in the PR body**; `pnpm run check`;
   `@copilot`; CI; squash. Close the bead. Say in the report that **the migration is the
   navigator's to run with the fleet down**, and that until they do, the running fleet keeps
   working on the old paths only while it runs the old cerebro.el.

## The test plan

- cerebro: `bash tests/agent-state.sh`, `tests/consumer-root.sh`, `tests/sync-symlinks.sh`,
  `tests/launchers.sh`; byte-compile; ERT.
- atlantis-hud: `pnpm run test:tooling` (the `cargoTargetDir` cases), `pnpm run check`.
- Human (navigator, after migrating): start an implementer from the fleet view — it claims, writes
  `.cerebro/state/<name>.state.json`, builds in `.cerebro/worktrees/<bead>`, `f` writes
  `.cerebro/state/<name>.stop` and it retires on `done`; `git status` clean throughout;
  `.claude/cerebro/scripts/prune-worktrees.sh --dry-run` lists the new directory. Psylocke marks
  this not-needed (harness only), and her own worktree is at the new path from her next pass.

## User-facing decisions

None a player sees. Navigator (2026-08-15): mount deferred; `.cerebro/state/`;
`.cerebro/worktrees/`; `.gitignore` ignores `.cerebro/` wholesale — each with the rejected
alternative in *Context*. P2 at triage, behind ah-e0w (merged).

## Out of scope

- Moving `.claude/cerebro` (the mount) — a later bead if wanted; root detection stays as is.
- A transition period reading both locations.
- Rewriting `docs/retrospectives/*` or the beads export in atlantis-hud.
- Any behaviour change in the fleet view or the scripts beyond the paths.

## Validation

```bash
# cerebro worktree
git grep -n 'claude/agents-state\|claude/worktrees\|claude/implementers' | grep -v '^docs/retrospectives' ; echo "(must print nothing)"
bash tests/agent-state.sh && bash tests/consumer-root.sh && bash tests/sync-symlinks.sh && bash tests/launchers.sh
emacs --batch -L emacs -f batch-byte-compile emacs/cerebro.el && emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
# atlantis-hud worktree
git grep -n 'claude/agents-state\|claude/worktrees\|claude/implementers' -- . ':!docs/retrospectives' ':!.beads' ':!.claude/cerebro'; echo "(must print nothing)"
diff CLAUDE.md .github/copilot-instructions.md && pnpm run check
```

## Known traps

- **Do not run the migration yourself, and do not `mv` a git worktree** — `git worktree move` or
  remove; the navigator runs it with the fleet down, from the PR body.
- **The fleet keeps running on the old cerebro.el until Emacs restarts** — merging PR 2 does not
  break anything by itself; the mismatch begins when a *new* session (new `agent-state`) writes to
  `.cerebro/state` while an *old* fleet view reads `.claude/agents-state`. Say so in the report and
  the PR body; the migration order above avoids it.
- **The `.claude/*` ignore block stays** — the mount and Claude's directories are still there; only
  the comment and the new `.cerebro/` line change.
- **`cargoTargetDir.ts`'s constant guards a trailing-slash rule** (`.cerebro-old` must still be a
  stray); keep the test that says so.
- **Two worktrees are live now on this machine** (`.claude/worktrees/psylocke`, and a scratch one
  outside the repository that is not the harness's) — the script above names Psylocke's; the
  scratch one is not moved.
- **Do not branch inside the shared `.claude/cerebro`**; cerebro worktree under (today)
  `.claude/worktrees/` with an absolute path — yes, this bead's own worktree lives at the old path;
  that is fine, it is removed when the PR merges.
acceptance_criteria: Agent state files, stop flags and agent worktrees live under .cerebro/ rather than .claude/. Claude Code's own discovery paths - .claude/agents/, .claude/skills/, .claude/settings.json - are untouched and the fleet still starts. The consumer's .gitignore covers the new location, so git status is clean while agents are running and prune-worktrees.sh still judges a worktree by its own cleanliness. Root detection still works in a fresh clone before any agent has run.

title: Refactoring: the fleet view wrestles vterm for a window; three rounds on one root cause
description:
## The cost being paid
vterm chooses its own window (pop-to-buffer-same-window), and the fleet view takes it back with a different mechanism per caller — display-buffer-overriding-action for the s keypress, save-window-excursion for a restart — selected by a boolean on cerebro--launch. Three rounds have been paid on the one root cause, the last a P0.

## Evidence
- cerebro 5fe8e83 sub-commit "Start an agent's session in the detail window, not the list window" — the session hid the list
- cerebro 5fe8e83 sub-commit "Scope the detail-window override, and stop it hiding the fleet" — "Adversarial review of the previous commit found three ways the override misbehaves, each with a real trigger"
- cerebro e6f4e4a fix(ah-aao): an automatic restart no longer steals the detail window (#13) — "An implementer's restart routed through cerebro--spawn-into-detail, which exists for the s keypress … it inherited an intention that was not its own"; adds cerebro--spawn-quietly / save-window-excursion and the quiet flag; bead ah-aao (P0)

## Where
.claude/cerebro/emacs/cerebro.el (cerebro--spawn-into-detail :913–957, cerebro--spawn-quietly :959–967, cerebro--launch :969)

## What a refactoring would change
One spawn that never lets vterm choose: create the buffer without displaying it (vterm's own buffer-creation without pop-to-buffer, or a display-buffer-alist rule for `*fleet: *` buffers), then place it — in the detail window when asked, nowhere when not — so both callers use one mechanism and no override or excursion is needed.

title: Refactoring: the fleet view has two render paths; the window-point fix was written twice
description:
## The cost being paid
The agent list (tabulated-list) and the bead panel (erase/insert) are two hand-rolled render paths, each with its own timer, its own selection-restore and its own window-point loop, so a fix to one does not reach the other — and the ERT suite renders into buffers that are never displayed, so a display-level defect passes green until the navigator sees it. The same defect (a timer render from another window leaves the visible window's point behind) was fixed in the bead panel, then had to be fixed again in the agent list as a P2 bug whose docstring says it mirrors the first fix.

## Evidence
- cerebro b0bbfaf sub-commit "Put the mark where the navigator can see it, not just where the buffer thinks" — set-window-point loop in cerebro--beads-render; its message: "The tests could not have caught this: every one of them rendered into a buffer that was never displayed, where buffer point is all there is"
- cerebro 800cce1 fix(ah-b8o): the fleet list keeps its selected agent across the 5s refresh (#10) — cerebro--sync-list-windows, "mirroring the same pattern already in cerebro--beads-render"; bead ah-b8o: "The bead panel had exactly this, found while building it… The agent list has no equivalent"
- Same test gap, another display defect fixed twice: 7f2dce0 changed the idle glyph's face, b0bbfaf "Make the idle dot an actual yellow dot" changed glyph and face again ("Verified before changing anything: the rendered buffer did carry the face on the glyph")

## Where
.claude/cerebro/emacs/cerebro.el (cerebro--beads-render :1410–1441, cerebro--sync-list-windows :1645–1654, cerebro--tick :1663); .claude/cerebro/emacs/cerebro-test.el (:194–217, :986–1057)

## What a refactoring would change
One render step both panels go through (render, restore selection, push point to every window) driven by one tick, and tests that display the buffer in a window before asserting on it, so a fix to how a refresh treats the visible window is written once and can be pinned.

title: Refactoring: fleet-view session ownership is a buffer-name regex; one failure fixed four times
description:
## The cost being paid
"Which sessions are mine" is derived by regexing vterm buffer names (cerebro--owned-buffer-agent-name, cerebro--owned), so any second vterm call for a name yields `*fleet: <name>*<2>` and an agent that is invisible for ever. The code defends that one failure in four separate places instead of at the source, and it still shipped as a real double-session bug when a state added in one guard was missed in another.

## Evidence
- cerebro 5fe8e83 sub-commit "Scope the detail-window override, and stop it hiding the fleet" — condition-case in cerebro--spawn-into-detail
- cerebro 5fe8e83 sub-commit "Make implementers interactive, and let Emacs supervise the one-bead loop" — kill-before-launch in cerebro--supervise
- cerebro 5fe8e83 sub-commit "Address the review: an owned session is alive whatever its file says" — cerebro--derive-implementer owned-but-no-file → idle
- cerebro 1bdfda7 feat(ah-u3i): "folds in a fix for cerebro--alive-p treating asking/done as dead (the `*fleet: <name>*<2>` double-session bug)" — the states added to derive in 5fe8e83 were missed in cerebro--alive-p's allow-list

## Where
.claude/cerebro/emacs/cerebro.el (cerebro--owned-buffer-agent-name :830, cerebro--owned :839, guards at :123, :643, :936, :1070)

## What a refactoring would change
Own the session handle rather than infer it: the fleet view records the buffer/process it started per name (a table keyed by name), and liveness, ownership and "already running" all read that one table — so a second launch is refused at the source and there is one predicate to keep in step with the state set.

title: Releases push main through a pre-push export gate that aborts, and retry around it
description:
## The cost being paid
The bead export is kept honest by a pre-push hook that commits on main and aborts the push, so everything else that pushes main — the release script above all — has to know the gate's contract and retry around it. Five fix/chore commits landed on the same interaction in three days; two releases were stranded at a bumped manifest with no tag and finished by hand; two release tags point at gate commits; twelve "chore(beads): refresh the issues export" commits sit on first-parent main; and two beads rewrote the same few lines of scripts/release.ts.

## Evidence
- 3293921 chore(ah-601): refresh the beads export at pre-push instead of every commit (#134)
- 6d1f5dc fix(ah-6xq.1): let only main carry the bead export (#141) — feature branches each carried a backlog snapshot and "whichever merged last reverted every close, claim, label and plan"
- 13c29b7 fix(ah-7go): settle the bead export before a release bumps anything (#148) — "meeting that abort after the version commit is what stranded v0.5.2 at a bumped manifest with no tag"
- 1cd99c3 fix(ah-r2e): retry a release push on the export gate's abort (#174) — v0.5.3 "failed exactly as v0.5.2 did and had to be finished by hand"; "tidying merged branches took four attempts"
- db24011 fix(ah-9dg): anchor the release tag to the release commit, not HEAD (#198); bead ah-9dg notes: "Both beads rewrite the same few lines of scripts/release.ts"
- git tag: v0.5.2 → 52ce64c chore(beads): refresh the issues export; v0.5.3 → b757b1d chore(beads): refresh the issues export

## Where
scripts/release.ts; scripts/releaseSupport.ts; scripts/beadsExportGate.ts; .beads/hooks/pre-push

## What a refactoring would change
One place that owns "push main" — the release script and the gate calling the same settle-then-push step, or the export refreshed by a workflow on the remote rather than a hook that fails the pusher — so a release is one push with no retry logic and no tag can land on a gate commit.

Filed by Bishop, weekly sweep of 2026-08-15 (first sweep, whole of origin/main), range e60bbbd..150ba17.
design:
## Context

`.beads/issues.jsonl` — the committed, readable export of the bead database — is kept fresh by a
**pre-push hook** (`scripts/beadsExportGate.ts`, run from `.beads/hooks/pre-push:59-68` outside
beads' own markers): on `main`, it exports, compares, and if stale **commits the refresh and aborts
the push** with "run the push again". A hook cannot amend the refs git has computed, so the abort is
inherent to the design — and everything else that pushes `main` has had to learn its contract: the
release script settles the export before bumping (ah-7go, after v0.5.2 was stranded at a bumped
manifest with no tag), retries the push on the gate's abort (ah-r2e, after v0.5.3 was stranded the
same way), and pins the tag's sha (ah-9dg, after v0.5.3's tag landed three commits above its
release). Five fixes on one seam in three days; two tags (`v0.5.2`, `v0.5.3`) point at
`chore(beads)` commits; twelve `chore(beads): refresh` commits on first-parent main; and
`scripts/releaseSupport.ts` grew `settleExport`, `pushWithRetry`, `isGateAbort`, `recoveryAdvice`.

Since squash-merges happen on GitHub, only two things ever push `main` from a machine: the release
script and the navigator's own hand-pushes (`git log --first-parent v0.5.3..` shows exactly those).
Settled with the navigator (2026-08-15): **the committed export is refreshed at release time only,
by the release script, as an ordinary commit before the version bump; the pre-push gate goes.**
Rejected: Cerebro refreshing it on its ten-minute sweep (a `chore(beads)` commit on main whenever the
backlog moved — many a day with four implementers); keeping the gate and only trimming the release
script (the abort-and-retry contract would remain for every hand-push). Between tags bd/Dolt is the
source of truth, as the beads-workflow skill already says ("never read it as truth").

After this bead: one push, no retry, no settle, no abort — the release commit follows the export
commit, the tag is pinned to the release commit as ah-9dg made it, and `releaseSupport.ts` loses the
gate machinery. **Where the code lives.** atlantis-hud (`scripts/`, `.beads/hooks/pre-push`,
`CLAUDE.md` pair, `docs/implementation-plan.md` line) — PR 1; cerebro (`skills/beads-workflow/SKILL.md`,
`agents/orchestrator.md`) — PR 2 — plus the bump. Line numbers against atlantis-hud `origin/main`
after #284 and cerebro `origin/main` `d05694b`+.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `scripts/beadsExportGate.ts` → `scripts/beadsExport.ts` (`git mv`)

Keep the two things worth keeping — `stableExport` (:55-103, the volatile-field normalisation, with
its tests) and the export/compare logic — and turn the module from a gate into **an exporter**:

```ts
export type ExportOutcome =
  | { kind: "unchanged" }
  | { kind: "refreshed"; committed: boolean }     // written; committed unless git refused
  | { kind: "skipped"; reason: "no-bd" | "no-beads" | "export-failed" };

/**
 * Refreshes .beads/issues.jsonl from the database and commits it as
 * "chore(beads): refresh the issues export" when it changed. Run by the release script before the
 * version bump (ah-cgk); never from a hook. Any branch: the caller decides where it runs.
 */
export function refreshBeadsExport(root: string): ExportOutcome;
```

- `decideGate`/`GateDecision` (:105-166) become `decideExport(input): { kind: "unchanged" } | { kind: "refresh"; text } | { kind: "skipped"; reason }` — the `detached-head` and `off-main` cases go (the caller, `release.ts`, has already refused a non-main branch at :150-158); the rest as today.
- `runGate` (:222-266) becomes `refreshBeadsExport`: write, `git diff --quiet HEAD -- <path>`, `git add`/`git commit --no-verify -m <REFRESH_MESSAGE>`; **no `process.exit`, no stderr contract about pushing again**; `PUSH_AGAIN_MESSAGE` deleted. The `invokedDirectly` block (:272-287) becomes a tiny CLI: `pnpm run beads:export` prints the outcome — for the navigator who wants a fresh export by hand (`package.json`: `"beads:export": "tsx scripts/beadsExport.ts"`).
- Header comment rewritten: why the export exists, why it is refreshed at release time only, why no
  branch but main should ever commit it (keep the ah-6xq.1 paragraph :16-20 verbatim), and that
  `export.auto` stays `false` in `.beads/config.yaml` (its comment at :75-77 → "refreshed by the
  release script").
- `scripts/beadsExportGate.test.ts` → `beadsExport.test.ts`: `stableExport` cases unchanged;
  `decideGate` cases → `decideExport` (drop `off-main`/`detached-head`; keep `no-bd`, `no-beads`,
  `export-failed`, `up-to-date`/`unchanged`, `refresh`).

### `.beads/hooks/pre-push`

Delete the block below the `END BEADS INTEGRATION` marker (:59-68). Beads' own section stays byte
for byte. Add nothing.

### `scripts/releaseSupport.ts` and `scripts/release.ts`

- Delete `settleStep`, `settleExport`, `Settlement` (:28-61), `isGateAbort`, `pushWithRetry`,
  `PushResult` (:111-146); `recoveryAdvice`/`ReleaseState` (:148-182) stay only if `finishRelease`
  still uses them for a *failed push* (it should: a push that fails for any reason must still say
  what state the release is in — bumped, tagged, pushed — and how to finish by hand); `finishRelease`
  (:202-…) drops `attempts` and the retry loop: create the tag on the pinned sha, push the branch
  once, push the tag once, report.
- `release.ts`: the *Settling the bead export* step (:207-230) becomes
  `const exported = refreshBeadsExport(root)` before the bump commit; log one line per outcome
  (`refreshed`: "release: refreshed the bead export (committed ahead of the bump)"; `unchanged`:
  nothing; `skipped`: "release: bead export skipped: <reason>" — a skip is not fatal, the release
  is not about the export). `PUSH_ATTEMPTS` (:75-80) and its comment go; the *pinned SHA* comment
  (:249-252) stays (ah-9dg). The header's mention of the gate (:50) is rewritten. `--dry-run` (:203)
  must not export or commit — check the order.
- `scripts/releaseSupport.test.ts`: delete the settle/retry cases; keep/adjust `finishRelease`
  (single push, tag pinned to the given sha, failure advice) and `describeGitFailure`.
- `scripts/releaseWorkflowGate.ts` — read it; if it references the export gate, adjust; probably not.

### Docs

- cerebro `skills/beads-workflow/SKILL.md`: *Storage* bullet (:303-307) — "refreshed by the release
  script at every release (`pnpm run release`), or by hand with `pnpm run beads:export` from main;
  never read it as truth"; delete *The export gate* (:315-337) and replace with three lines
  (*The committed export*: when it is refreshed, why no branch but main commits it — keep the
  ah-6xq.1 paragraph); the *Traps* mention (:344-351) → point at `beads:export`.
- cerebro `agents/orchestrator.md` *Cutting a release* (:616-…): if it mentions the gate's abort or
  "push again" (grep `again\|gate\|export`), reword: the release refreshes the export itself.
- atlantis-hud `CLAUDE.md:348` (`.beads/issues.jsonl is a readable export that is committed`) → "…
  committed, refreshed by the release script"; mirror in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.
  `docs/implementation-plan.md:40` fine as is.

## Increments

1. RED: `beadsExport.test.ts` (`decideExport` without the branch cases; `refreshBeadsExport`
   outcomes with a temp git repo — the existing test file's fixtures show how; if none, `mkdtemp` +
   `git init` as `scripts/cargoTargetDir.test.ts` does). GREEN: the rename and rewrite; hook block
   removed; `package.json` script.
2. RED: `releaseSupport.test.ts` trimmed to the single-push `finishRelease`; GREEN: `releaseSupport.ts`,
   `release.ts` (`--dry-run` still writes nothing).
3. Docs in atlantis-hud; PR 1 `refactor(ah-cgk): the bead export is refreshed by the release script,
   not by a pre-push gate`; `@copilot`; CI; squash. Then cerebro PR 2 (skill + orchestrator wording),
   bump PR 3.
4. **Do not cut a release to validate** — `pnpm run release --dry-run` from main is the check; the
   next real release (Cerebro's) is the proof, and the plan says so in the PR body.

## The test plan

- `pnpm run test:tooling` (`beadsExport.test.ts`, `releaseSupport.test.ts`, `releaseWorkflowGate.test.ts`,
  `ciDocsGate.test.ts`), `pnpm run typecheck:tooling`, `pnpm run check`.
- Manual: `pnpm run beads:export` on a clean main → prints the outcome, commits only if changed;
  `pnpm run release --dry-run` → no writes; a `git push` of main no longer runs the gate (`git push
  --dry-run origin main` shows no `beads:` lines).

## User-facing decisions

None a player sees. Navigator (2026-08-15): export refreshed at release time only, by the release
script; the pre-push gate removed (rejected alternatives in *Context*).

## Out of scope

- Any change to how beads sync (`bd dolt push/pull`), the Dolt remote, or `export.auto`.
- Cerebro's release *procedure* beyond the wording that mentioned the gate.
- Rewriting the two historical tags.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run test:tooling && pnpm run typecheck:tooling
pnpm run beads:export            # on main: "unchanged" or one chore(beads) commit
pnpm run release --dry-run patch # writes nothing
grep -n 'beadsExportGate' -r scripts .beads/hooks CLAUDE.md .github docs   # nothing
pnpm run check
```

Human check: none; Psylocke marks not-needed. The next release Cerebro cuts is the live proof —
tag on the release commit, one push, no retry.

## Known traps

- **`.beads/hooks/pre-push` is committed** and `bd hooks install` rewrites only its marker section —
  delete our block by hand and leave the markers intact; do not run `bd hooks install`.
- **`git commit --no-verify`** in the exporter stays (a pre-commit hook must not recurse into
  anything); the export commit is made on whatever branch the caller is on — `release.ts` has
  already required `main`; `beads:export` by hand should refuse off `main` (keep an `off-main`
  refusal in the CLI wrapper, not in the library — say so).
- **`stableExport` normalisation is what keeps the release from committing a refresh on every run**
  (lease fields churn every minute) — keep it and its tests.
- **`--dry-run` ordering** in `release.ts`: the export refresh must sit after the dry-run exit
  (:203) or a dry run would commit.
- **Do not branch inside the shared `.claude/cerebro`** for PR 2; worktrees under
  `.claude/worktrees/` (absolute path for the cerebro one).

title: Refactoring: map view ownership is split across two components; restore was delivered twice
description:
## The cost being paid
"Where the map is" is owned in two places — MapCanvas owns pan/zoom/framing, AppShell owns level and selected hex — both writing one localStorage record, and correctness rests on four refs plus effect definition order ("This effect runs before the frame effect (effects fire in definition order), which is what makes the restore win"). Viewport persistence had to be delivered twice: the first restore was overwritten a moment later by two other effects, the second PR's review found a third defect in the same mechanism, and the storage had to become read-modify-write so the two halves would stop undoing each other.

## Evidence
- bc9957c "Persist map viewport (pan + zoom) per game across sessions (#65)"
- 45b29be feat(ah-ppd): reopen a game on the map view it was left at (#137) — "were then overwritten a moment later, twice over": the selection-follow effect pulled the pan back to the opening hex, and the model-keyed re-frame threw the position away on every import; PR #137 review: "restoredRegionRef outlived the selection it described … keepsRestoredHex now ends the exemption"
- packages/shared/src/workspace/mapViewRestore.ts:1–9: "A plain module rather than logic inside the component, because this decision has been wrong twice and neither mistake was visible in anything that renders"
- packages/shared/src/workspace/mapViewportStorage.ts:8–11: read-modify-write "because the two halves change at different moments … or each would keep undoing the other's half of the view"

## Where
packages/shared/src/workspace/MapCanvas.tsx (viewRef/framedRef/pendingRestoreRef/restoredRegionRef :168–215, effects :359–449); mapViewRestore.ts; mapViewportStorage.ts; AppShell.tsx (enterGame :1729–1780, saveFocusForGame effect :575–582)

## What a refactoring would change
One owner of the map view (level, pan, zoom, selection) as one piece of state with one persistence step, MapCanvas rendering it rather than holding half of it in refs, so restore-vs-frame-vs-follow is a decision made once in plain code (as mapViewRestore.ts started to do) rather than by effect ordering.

Filed by Bishop, weekly sweep of 2026-08-15 (first sweep, whole of origin/main), range e60bbbd..150ba17.

title: Refactoring: the map's one-shot fit reads live pane boxes; two plans misread it, one paid 2h
description:
## The cost being paid
MapCanvas's initial fit is computed once from the live DOM boxes of whatever [data-map-overlay] panes are mounted at that instant, then held (framedRef → "hold"); its ResizeObserver watches only the host. So any panel's default footprint silently re-tiers the initial zoom, nothing exposes the "visible strip" to tests, and two plans read the mechanism as continuous when it is one-shot. One implementer paid about two hours when a bigger default units pane pushed the fit from map-mid to map-far and broke two smoke tests that never touch the pane; another paid 25 minutes recomputing the visible centre in a test, and that inset arithmetic is now duplicated in two smoke specs.

## Evidence
- docs/retrospectives/ah-2r3.md §"A bigger default units pane pushed the map's initial fit out a zoom tier, breaking two unrelated smoke tests" — "About two hours"; fixed by explicit zoom/pan in 3d44bf1's tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts hunk
- docs/retrospectives/ah-t2i.md §"A gesture that recentres the view is not idempotent at a fixed screen pixel" — "About 25 minutes … the side panes' insets are asymmetric enough that using box.width/2, box.height/2 picked a point covered by a panel header"; the arithmetic now lives in tests/smoke/shortcuts.spec.ts:222–247 (visibleCentre) and tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts:2477–2510
- Two plans misread it the same way: bead ah-3cs design "feeds mapOverlayInsets.ts and re-fits the map"; bead ah-2r3 design "MapCanvas observes every [data-map-overlay] with a ResizeObserver (MapCanvas.tsx:329, 345) and refits the map — dragging the units pane refits continuously" — the observer at :340–353 observes host only; framedRef/hold at :376–404
- bead ah-t2i design "Known traps": "readInsets() matters … the keyboard cursor path does not [pass insets], a known inconsistency — do not copy it" (MapCanvas.tsx:646–647 vs :434, :532, :783, :1032)

## Where
packages/shared/src/workspace/MapCanvas.tsx (readInsets :322–335, observer :340–353, frame effect :372–408, keyboard path :646–647); packages/shared/src/workspace/mapOverlayInsets.ts; packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx (:2889–3025 data-map-overlay markers)

## What a refactoring would change
The visible strip made an explicit input — the shell computes insets from its own layout state (which panes are open and how tall) and passes them to MapCanvas, which fits against that and re-fits when it changes — with the strip exposed for tests, so a pane's default cannot silently move the zoom tier and every pointer path (keyboard included) uses the same insets.
